categories.title: Slurry, manure and agricultural effluent management
categories.description: Slurry, manure, and agricultural effluent management covering storage, spreading, and disposal of livestock waste including pig slurry, poultry manure, farmyard manure (FYM), liquid manure, silage effluent, and digestate. Covers storage infrastructure requirements such as slurry tanks, lagoons, slurry stores, reception pits, lined lagoons, freeboard, structural integrity, and secondary containment. Includes land application controls covering application rates, buffer zones, closed periods, and muck spreading. Covers environmental protection requirements including ammonia emissions, runoff prevention.

legislation.name: The Reduction and Prevention of Agricultural Diffuse Pollution (England) Regulations 2018
The Water Resources (Control of Agricultural Pollution) (Wales) Regulations 2021
The Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (Scotland) Regulations 2003
The Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (England) Regulations 2010

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations may be cited as the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2015.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Citation
legislation_propositions.label: Citation

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations come into force on 1st May 2015.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Commencement date
legislation_propositions.label: Commencement date

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations apply in relation to England only.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Territorial application
legislation_propositions.label: Territorial application

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Parts 3 to 8 apply only in relation to holdings that are in nitrate vulnerable zones designated for the purposes of these Regulations.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Application to nitrate vulnerable zones
legislation_propositions.label: Application to nitrate vulnerable zones

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry is defined as excreta produced by livestock (other than poultry) while in a yard or building (including any bedding, rainwater or washings mixed with it) that has a consistency that allows it to be pumped or discharged by gravity; in the case of excreta separated into its liquid and solid fractions, the slurry is the liquid fraction.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of slurry
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of slurry

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Organic manure is defined as a nitrogen fertiliser or phosphate fertiliser derived from animal, plant or human sources and includes livestock manure.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of organic manure
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of organic manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Agricultural has the meaning given by section 109(3) of the Agriculture Act 1947.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of agricultural (cross-reference)
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of agricultural (cross-reference)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Spreading, in relation to land, includes applying to the surface of the land, injecting into the land or mixing with the surface layers of the land, but does not include the direct deposit of excreta on to land by animals.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An area is designated as a nitrate vulnerable zone if it is land that drains into polluted waters, contributes to the pollution of those waters, and is marked as such a zone on a relevant map.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Designation of nitrate vulnerable zones
legislation_propositions.label: Designation of nitrate vulnerable zones

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For the period from 1 December 2016 until the Secretary of State next revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones under regulation 4(5), 'relevant map' means a map marked 'Nitrate Vulnerable Zones (England) 2017 to 2020' published on 1 December 2016 on the Agency's website.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of relevant map (initial period)
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of relevant map (initial period)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Following any subsequent review under regulation 4(5), 'relevant map' means a map published on the Agency's website that is marked 'This map identifies those areas of England designated by the Secretary of State as a Nitrate Vulnerable Zone for the purposes of the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2015 (England)' and specifies the period to which it relates.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of relevant map (post-review)
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of relevant map (post-review)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Agency must make provision for a relevant map to be obtainable by persons without access to the internet.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to provide offline access to maps
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to provide offline access to maps

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Secretary of State must keep under review the eutrophic state of fresh surface waters, estuarial waters and coastal waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to review eutrophic state of waters
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to review eutrophic state of waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Secretary of State must, before 1st January 2017 and before 1st January of every fourth year thereafter, monitor the nitrate concentration in freshwaters over a period of one year at sampling stations representative of surface water at least monthly and more frequently during flood periods.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to monitor nitrate concentration in surface water
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to monitor nitrate concentration in surface water

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No later than the end of each four-year period, the Secretary of State must identify water affected by pollution or that could be if controls are not applied, identify land draining into those waters that contributes to pollution, take into account changes and factors unforeseen at the time of previous designation, and if necessary revise or add to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to identify polluted waters and designate nitrate vulnerable zones
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to identify polluted waters and designate nitrate vulnerable zones

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Agency must make recommendations to the Secretary of State before 10th August 2016 and before 10th August of every fourth year thereafter as to which areas of land should be, or should continue to be, designated as nitrate vulnerable zones, by reference to the matters in regulation 4(5)(a) to (c).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Agency duty: quadrennial NVZ recommendations
legislation_propositions.label: Agency duty: quadrennial NVZ recommendations

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In deciding whether to revise or add to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones for the purposes of regulation 4(5)(d), the Secretary of State must have regard to the recommendations made by the Agency under regulation 5(1).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Secretary of State duty: regard to Agency recommendations
legislation_propositions.label: Secretary of State duty: regard to Agency recommendations

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before revising or adding to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones (except where paragraph (3A) applies), the Secretary of State must publish the proposals to revise or add to the designation and send written notice to any person appearing to be the owner or occupier of a relevant holding.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Secretary of State duty: publication and notice (general)
legislation_propositions.label: Secretary of State duty: publication and notice (general)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where the Secretary of State revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones before 1st January 2017, the Secretary of State must by 31st December 2016 publish the proposals on the Agency's website and by 1st March 2017 send written notice to any person appearing to be the owner or occupier of a relevant holding.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Secretary of State duty: transitional publication and notice (pre-2017)
legislation_propositions.label: Secretary of State duty: transitional publication and notice (pre-2017)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The requirements of the regulations listed in Schedule 4 do not apply in relation to a new holding until the dates set out in that Schedule.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Transitional exemption for new holdings from Schedule 4 requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Transitional exemption for new holdings from Schedule 4 requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An owner or occupier of a relevant holding who is sent a notice under regulation 5(3)(b) or 5(3A)(b) may appeal to the First-tier Tribunal against the proposals or designation referred to in the notice.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Right of appeal to First-tier Tribunal for owners/occupiers of relevant holdings
legislation_propositions.label: Right of appeal to First-tier Tribunal for owners/occupiers of relevant holdings

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The only grounds of appeal under regulation 6 are that the relevant holding (or any part of it) does not drain into water which the Secretary of State proposes to identify, or to continue to identify, as polluted or which has been similarly identified in Wales or Scotland, or in a case within regulation 5(3A), does not drain into water which the Secretary of State has identified as polluted or which has been similarly identified in Wales or Scotland.
legislation_propositions.short_name: First ground of appeal: holding does not drain into polluted water
legislation_propositions.label: First ground of appeal: holding does not drain into polluted water

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The only grounds of appeal under regulation 6 include that the relevant holding (or any part of it) drains into water which the Secretary of State should not identify, or should not continue to identify, as polluted.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Second ground of appeal: water should not be identified as polluted
legislation_propositions.label: Second ground of appeal: water should not be identified as polluted

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If the First-tier Tribunal upholds an appeal under paragraph (2)(b), the Secretary of State, when acting under regulation 4(5), must treat the water concerned as water which should not be identified, or should not continue to be identified, as polluted, and treat any holding (or part of any holding) which drains into that water accordingly regardless of whether the owner or occupier of the relevant holding appealed.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effect of successful appeal on ground (2)(b): water de-designation and consequential treatment of all holdings
legislation_propositions.label: Effect of successful appeal on ground (2)(b): water de-designation and consequential treatment of all holdings

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a holding must ensure that the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure applied to the holding in any calendar year does not exceed 170kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Annual nitrogen limit from livestock manure
legislation_propositions.label: Annual nitrogen limit from livestock manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The nitrogen limit does not apply where the occupier has been granted a derogation.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Derogation exception to nitrogen limit
legislation_propositions.label: Derogation exception to nitrogen limit

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In calculating the area of a holding for nitrogen spreading limits, no account is to be taken of surface waters, hardstanding, buildings, roads, or woodland (unless used for grazing).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exclusion of certain land types from area calculation
legislation_propositions.label: Exclusion of certain land types from area calculation

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In calculating the area of a holding for nitrogen spreading limits, no account is to be taken of land covered by a greenhouse for the whole of the year concerned.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exclusion of year-round greenhouse land from area calculation
legislation_propositions.label: Exclusion of year-round greenhouse land from area calculation

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a holding must ensure that in any twelve-month period, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure spread on any given hectare of land on the holding does not exceed 250kg.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Nitrogen limit in organic manure: 250kg per hectare per year
legislation_propositions.label: Nitrogen limit in organic manure: 250kg per hectare per year

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier may exceed the 250kg nitrogen limit if organic manure is in the form of certified green compost or certified green/food compost, the total nitrogen in such compost does not exceed 500kg per hectare in any two-year period (or 1,000kg per hectare in any four-year period for orchard land spread as mulch), and no other form of organic manure is spread over the land during the applicable period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for certified green compost: higher nitrogen limits apply
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for certified green compost: higher nitrogen limits apply

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Regulation 8 does not apply where at least 80% of the holding's agricultural area is sown with grass, the total nitrogen in organic manure applied to the holding does not exceed 100kg multiplied by the area in hectares, the total nitrogen from manufactured nitrogen fertiliser does not exceed 90kg multiplied by the area in hectares, the occupier does not bring organic manure onto the holding, and the occupier makes a record demonstrating these requirements are met.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Grassland exemption: alternative nitrogen regime for holdings with 80%+ grass
legislation_propositions.label: Grassland exemption: alternative nitrogen regime for holdings with 80%+ grass

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For the purposes of regulation 8, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure is to be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 14, and the reference to land on the holding does not include any land which is covered by a greenhouse for the whole of the period concerned.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Calculation method and greenhouse exclusion for nitrogen limits
legislation_propositions.label: Calculation method and greenhouse exclusion for nitrogen limits

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Part 3 does not apply to the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser on a crop growing in a greenhouse.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exemption: nitrogen fertiliser spreading in greenhouses
legislation_propositions.label: Exemption: nitrogen fertiliser spreading in greenhouses

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the soil likely to be available for crop uptake during the growing season, calculate the optimum amount of nitrogen to be spread taking that soil nitrogen into account, and produce a fertilisation plan.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to calculate soil nitrogen, optimum nitrogen amount, and produce fertilisation plan before spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to calculate soil nitrogen, optimum nitrogen amount, and produce fertilisation plan before spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the fertilisation planning duty each calendar year before the first spreading of nitrogen fertiliser.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Annual fertilisation planning duty for permanent grassland
legislation_propositions.label: Annual fertilisation planning duty for permanent grassland

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For any crop other than permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the fertilisation planning duty before spreading nitrogen fertiliser for the first time for a crop planted or intended to be planted.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fertilisation planning duty for non-permanent grassland crops
legislation_propositions.label: Fertilisation planning duty for non-permanent grassland crops

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The fertilisation plan must be in permanent form and must record the field reference or name, the area planted or intended to be planted, the crop type, soil type, previous crop details, the calculated soil nitrogen amount and calculation method, expected planting month, expected yield (if arable), and the optimum nitrogen amount.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Mandatory content and form requirements for fertilisation plans
legislation_propositions.label: Mandatory content and form requirements for fertilisation plans

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before spreading organic manure, the occupier of a holding must on each occasion calculate the amount of nitrogen that is likely to be available from that manure for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Calculation of available nitrogen before spreading organic manure
legislation_propositions.label: Calculation of available nitrogen before spreading organic manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before spreading organic manure, the occupier of a holding must record the area on which the manure is to be spread, the quantity to be spread, the month in which it is to be spread, the type of manure, its total nitrogen content, and the amount of nitrogen likely to be available from the manure to be spread for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Recording requirements before spreading organic manure
legislation_propositions.label: Recording requirements before spreading organic manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must record the amount required and the month in which it is planned to spread it.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Recording requirements before spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser
legislation_propositions.label: Recording requirements before spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An occupier of a holding may, acting on written advice of a FACTS adviser, spread nitrogen on grass grown for minimum 16% protein content in amounts exceeding regulation 12 limits, subject to absolute caps.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Derogation for high-protein grass: FACTS-advised nitrogen spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Derogation for high-protein grass: FACTS-advised nitrogen spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The total amount of nitrogen spread on any given hectare of high-protein grass must not exceed 700 kg if irrigated or 500 kg if not irrigated.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Absolute nitrogen caps for high-protein grass
legislation_propositions.label: Absolute nitrogen caps for high-protein grass

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For high-protein grass nitrogen spreading, the total amount of nitrogen from organic manure must be calculated by reference to the methods for establishing available nitrogen described in regulation 14.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Calculation method for organic manure nitrogen
legislation_propositions.label: Calculation method for organic manure nitrogen

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: After relying on the high-protein grass derogation, the occupier must provide the FACTS adviser with soil analyses from representative autumn soil samples (taken 1 September to 31 October) so the adviser may take them into account when advising for subsequent years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Post-spreading soil analysis obligation
legislation_propositions.label: Post-spreading soil analysis obligation

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For livestock manure, nitrogen content must be calculated either by using the standard table in Part 1 of Schedule 2 or by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of that Schedule.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Livestock manure nitrogen content calculation methods
legislation_propositions.label: Livestock manure nitrogen content calculation methods

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For cattle slurry spread on or after 1st January 2014, the available nitrogen is 40% of the nitrogen content.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Cattle slurry available nitrogen percentage (post-2014)
legislation_propositions.label: Cattle slurry available nitrogen percentage (post-2014)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For pig slurry spread on or after 1st January 2014, the available nitrogen is 50% of the nitrogen content.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Pig slurry available nitrogen percentage (post-2014)
legislation_propositions.label: Pig slurry available nitrogen percentage (post-2014)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An occupier may not spread organic manure on a crop referred to in regulation 12 or 13 if no nitrogen value is established for that manure for the purposes of regulations 8(9), 12(2), 13(4) or 31(6).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on spreading organic manure without established nitrogen values
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on spreading organic manure without established nitrogen values

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure on that holding must produce and maintain a risk map showing each field with its area in hectares, all surface waters, any boreholes, springs or wells on the holding or within 50 metres of the boundary, areas with sandy or shallow soils, land with an incline greater than 12 degrees, land within 10 metres of surface waters, land within 50 metres of a borehole, spring or well, land drains (other than sealed impermeable pipes), sites suitable for temporary field heaps if this storage method is to be used, and land that has a low run-off risk.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to produce and maintain risk map for organic manure spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to produce and maintain risk map for organic manure spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Information on land that has a low run-off risk need not be included in a risk map produced by an occupier who does not intend to spread manure on such land during the storage period referred to in regulation 25.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for low run-off risk land information in risk map
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for low run-off risk land information in risk map

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where a change in circumstances affects a matter referred to in the risk map requirements, the occupier must update the risk map within three months of the change.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to update risk map within three months of relevant change
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to update risk map within three months of relevant change

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must keep a copy of the risk map for the holding.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to retain copy of risk map
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to retain copy of risk map

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must undertake a field inspection to consider the risk of nitrogen getting into surface water.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Pre-spreading field inspection duty
legislation_propositions.label: Pre-spreading field inspection duty

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person must not spread nitrogen fertiliser on land if there is a significant risk of nitrogen getting into surface water, taking into account slope (especially if greater than 12 degrees), ground cover, proximity to surface water, weather conditions, soil type, and presence of land drains.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on spreading where significant risk to surface water
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on spreading where significant risk to surface water

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person must not spread nitrogen fertiliser if the soil is waterlogged, flooded, snow covered, or has been frozen for more than 12 hours in the previous 24 hours.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on spreading in adverse soil conditions
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on spreading in adverse soil conditions

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person must not spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser within 2 metres of surface water.
legislation_propositions.short_name: 2-metre buffer zone for manufactured nitrogen fertiliser
legislation_propositions.label: 2-metre buffer zone for manufactured nitrogen fertiliser

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person must not spread organic manure within 10 metres of surface water, except where permitted by specific exceptions for livestock manure or slurry/sewage sludge/anaerobic digestate with appropriate equipment.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on spreading organic manure within 10 metres of surface water
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on spreading organic manure within 10 metres of surface water

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure) may be spread within 10 metres of surface water if it is spread on land managed for breeding wader birds or as species-rich semi-natural grassland that is notified as a site of special scientific interest or subject to an agri-environmental commitment, during the period 1st June to 31st October, not directly on surface water, and the total annual amount does not exceed 12.5 tonnes per hectare.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for livestock manure on designated conservation land
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for livestock manure on designated conservation land

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Organic manure in the form of slurry, sewage sludge or anaerobic digestate may be spread within 10 metres but not within 6 metres of surface water if the spreading equipment used is a trailing hose band spreader, a trailing shoe band spreader, an injector which injects the organic manure no deeper than 10cm below the surface of the soil, or a dribble bar applicator.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for slurry, sewage sludge and anaerobic digestate with specified equipment
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for slurry, sewage sludge and anaerobic digestate with specified equipment

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person must not spread organic manure within 50 metres of a borehole, spring or well.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on spreading organic manure within 50 metres of water sources
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on spreading organic manure within 50 metres of water sources

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Equipment used to spread slurry by broadcasting must have a trajectory of less than 4 metres from the ground.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry broadcasting equipment: low-trajectory requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry broadcasting equipment: low-trajectory requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Equipment used to spread slurry by broadcasting that has a trajectory of 4 metres or more from the ground must be able to achieve a maximum slurry application rate of 1 mm per hour when operating continuously.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry broadcasting equipment: high-trajectory application rate limit
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry broadcasting equipment: high-trajectory application rate limit

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person who applies organic manure on to the surface of bare soil or stubble (other than soil that has been sown) must ensure that it is incorporated into the soil in accordance with this regulation.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to incorporate organic manure applied to bare soil or stubble
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to incorporate organic manure applied to bare soil or stubble

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Poultry manure applied to bare soil or stubble must be incorporated as soon as practicable and within 24 hours at the latest.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Incorporation timeframe for poultry manure
legislation_propositions.label: Incorporation timeframe for poultry manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry or liquid from the treatment of sewage sludge by anaerobic digestion must be incorporated as soon as practicable and within 24 hours at the latest, unless it was applied using equipment described in regulation 17(4)(a) or (c) or an injector which injects the organic manure into the ground.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Incorporation timeframe for slurry and liquid digestate
legislation_propositions.label: Incorporation timeframe for slurry and liquid digestate

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Any other organic manure (other than organic manure spread as a mulch on sandy soil) must be incorporated as soon as practicable and within 24 hours at the latest, if the land is within 50 metres of surface water and slopes in such a way that there may be a run-off to that water.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Incorporation timeframe for other organic manure near surface water on sloping land
legislation_propositions.label: Incorporation timeframe for other organic manure near surface water on sloping land

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person must not spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on land during the closed period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on spreading organic manure with high readily available nitrogen during closed period
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on spreading organic manure with high readily available nitrogen during closed period

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on tillage land with sandy or shallow soil during the period from 1st August to 15th September if the next crop sown on the land is sown on or before 15th September.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for tillage land with sandy or shallow soil (1 Aug–15 Sep)
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for tillage land with sandy or shallow soil (1 Aug–15 Sep)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Between the end of the closed period and the end of the following February, the maximum amount of slurry that may be spread at any one time is 30 cubic metres per hectare.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Maximum slurry spreading limit (30 m³/ha) post-closed period
legislation_propositions.label: Maximum slurry spreading limit (30 m³/ha) post-closed period

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Between the end of the closed period and the end of the following February, there must be at least three weeks between any spreading of slurry or poultry manure.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum three-week interval between spreading events post-closed period
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum three-week interval between spreading events post-closed period

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An occupier of a holding under the organic control system may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on winter oilseed rape, asparagus, brassica, grass, over-wintered salad onions, parsley or bulb onions during the closed period, or on any other crop if in accordance with written advice from a FACTS adviser.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Organic holdings: derogation for spreading high readily available nitrogen manure on specified crops
legislation_propositions.label: Organic holdings: derogation for spreading high readily available nitrogen manure on specified crops

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In the case of winter oilseed rape under the organic holding derogation, nitrogen must not be spread after 31st October.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Winter oilseed rape: nitrogen spreading deadline
legislation_propositions.label: Winter oilseed rape: nitrogen spreading deadline

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In the case of brassica under the organic holding derogation, an additional 50kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread every four weeks during the closed period up to harvest, provided the 150kg total nitrogen limit is not exceeded.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Brassica: additional nitrogen allowance during closed period
legislation_propositions.label: Brassica: additional nitrogen allowance during closed period

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In the case of grass under the organic holding derogation, nitrogen must not be spread after 31st October and a maximum of 40kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread at any one time.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Grass: nitrogen spreading deadline and single-application limit
legislation_propositions.label: Grass: nitrogen spreading deadline and single-application limit

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person must not spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser on land during the closed period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser during closed period
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser during closed period

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The closed period for grassland begins with 15th September and ends with the following 15th January.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Closed period definition for grassland
legislation_propositions.label: Closed period definition for grassland

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The closed period for tillage land begins with 1st September and ends with the following 15th January.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Closed period definition for tillage land
legislation_propositions.label: Closed period definition for tillage land

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person may spread fertiliser during the closed period on a crop specified in the table if the rate of nitrogen specified in the second column is not exceeded.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for specified crops during closed period
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for specified crops during closed period

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A heap of solid manure forming a temporary field site must occupy as small a surface area as is practically required to support the mass of the heap and prevent it from collapse.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Surface area requirement for solid manure heaps on temporary field sites
legislation_propositions.label: Surface area requirement for solid manure heaps on temporary field sites

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Solid poultry manure that does not have bedding mixed into it and is stored on a temporary field site must be covered with an impermeable material.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Covering requirement for solid poultry manure on temporary field sites
legislation_propositions.label: Covering requirement for solid poultry manure on temporary field sites

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a relevant holding must separate slurry mechanically or on an impermeable surface where the liquid drains into a suitable receptacle.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry separation method requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry separation method requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An occupier of a holding who keeps specified animals must provide sufficient storage for all slurry produced on the holding during the storage period and for all poultry manure produced in a yard or building on the holding during the storage period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to provide slurry and poultry manure storage
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to provide slurry and poultry manure storage

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry store must have the capacity to store, in addition to the manure, any rainfall, washings or other liquid that enters the vessel (either directly or indirectly) during the storage period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry store capacity for additional liquids
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry store capacity for additional liquids

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Storage facilities are not necessary for slurry or poultry manure that the occupier intends will be sent off the holding or spread in accordance with these Regulations on land that has a low run-off risk.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception to storage requirement for off-holding or low run-off spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Exception to storage requirement for off-holding or low run-off spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where slurry or poultry manure is intended to be spread on land with a low run-off risk, storage facilities for an additional one week's manure must be provided as a contingency measure in the event of spreading not being possible on some dates.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Contingency storage for low run-off spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Contingency storage for low run-off spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a new holding must record the total size of the holding, calculated in accordance with regulation 7(4).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to record total size of new holding
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to record total size of new holding

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a new holding with livestock must calculate and record the amount of manure that will be produced by the number of animals expected to be kept in a building or on hardstanding during the storage period, using the figures in Schedule 1.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Calculation and recording of manure production for new holdings
legislation_propositions.label: Calculation and recording of manure production for new holdings

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a new holding with livestock must calculate and record the amount of storage capacity (in slurry vessels and hardstanding) required to enable compliance with regulation 25, taking into account the amount of manure intended to be exported from the holding, the amount of manure intended to be spread on land that has a low run-off risk, and in the case of a slurry vessel, the amount of liquids other than slurry likely to enter the vessel.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Calculation and recording of required storage capacity for new holdings
legislation_propositions.label: Calculation and recording of required storage capacity for new holdings

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a new holding with livestock must calculate and record the current storage capacity of the holding.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Recording of current storage capacity for new holdings
legislation_propositions.label: Recording of current storage capacity for new holdings

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before 30th April each year, the occupier of a holding with livestock must record for the previous storage period the number of animals in a building or hardstanding on the holding during that period and the category for each animal by reference to Schedule 1.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Annual livestock record-keeping obligation
legislation_propositions.label: Annual livestock record-keeping obligation

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must also record the temporary field sites used for free-standing heaps as referred to in regulation 23 and the dates of use.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Temporary field site record-keeping obligation
legislation_propositions.label: Temporary field site record-keeping obligation

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In regulation 26, 'storage period' has the meaning given in regulation 25(7).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of storage period for record-keeping
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of storage period for record-keeping

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a holding with livestock must, before 30th April each year, record the number of animals on the holding during the previous calendar year and the category for each animal by reference to Schedule 1, and the number of days that each animal spent on the holding.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Annual livestock record-keeping obligation
legislation_propositions.label: Annual livestock record-keeping obligation

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the manure produced by the animals on the holding during that year by reference to Schedule 1.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Nitrogen calculation obligation
legislation_propositions.label: Nitrogen calculation obligation

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In the case of permanently housed pigs or poultry, the occupier may use software approved by the Secretary of State or, in the case of a system of keeping livestock that only produces solid manure, sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 2, as an alternative to the method referred to in paragraph (2).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Alternative nitrogen calculation methods for permanently housed pigs or poultry
legislation_propositions.label: Alternative nitrogen calculation methods for permanently housed pigs or poultry

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must make a record of the calculations and how the final figures were arrived at, and where the occupier uses software approved by the Secretary of State, the occupier must keep a printout of the result.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record-keeping of nitrogen calculations and software outputs
legislation_propositions.label: Record-keeping of nitrogen calculations and software outputs

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An occupier of a holding who brings livestock manure onto the holding must, within one week, record the type and amount of livestock manure, the date it was brought on, the nitrogen content (if known), and the name and address of the supplier.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record-keeping for livestock manure brought onto holding
legislation_propositions.label: Record-keeping for livestock manure brought onto holding

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week, record the type and amount of livestock manure, the date it was sent off, the nitrogen content, the name and address of the recipient, and details of a contingency plan in the event that an agreement for a person to accept the livestock manure fails.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record-keeping for livestock manure sent off holding
legislation_propositions.label: Record-keeping for livestock manure sent off holding

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If the nitrogen content of livestock manure brought onto a holding is not known, the occupier must ascertain it as soon as reasonably practicable after arrival and record it within one week of ascertaining it.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to ascertain and record unknown nitrogen content
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to ascertain and record unknown nitrogen content

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For the purposes of ascertaining nitrogen content, it must be determined either by using the standard figures in Part 1 of Schedule 2 or by sampling and analysis as set out in Part 2 of that Schedule.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Methods for ascertaining nitrogen content
legislation_propositions.label: Methods for ascertaining nitrogen content

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person using sampling and analysis to determine nitrogen content in organic manure must keep the original laboratory report.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to retain original laboratory report for nitrogen content analysis in organic manure
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to retain original laboratory report for nitrogen content analysis in organic manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a holding must, within one week of sowing a crop on which nitrogen fertiliser is spread or intended to be spread, record the crop sown and the date of sowing.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record-keeping obligation for nitrogen fertiliser application on crops
legislation_propositions.label: Record-keeping obligation for nitrogen fertiliser application on crops

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The record-keeping obligation for crops on which nitrogen fertiliser is spread does not apply to a crop growing in a greenhouse.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Greenhouse exception to crop record-keeping
legislation_propositions.label: Greenhouse exception to crop record-keeping

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure must, within one week of doing so, record the area spread, the quantity of organic manure spread, the date, the method, the type of organic manure, the total nitrogen content, and the amount of nitrogen that was available to the crop.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record-keeping obligation for organic manure spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Record-keeping obligation for organic manure spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a holding must, within one week of spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, record the date of spreading and the amount of nitrogen spread.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record-keeping obligation for manufactured nitrogen fertiliser spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Record-keeping obligation for manufactured nitrogen fertiliser spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Regulation 31 does not apply to nitrogen fertiliser spread in a greenhouse.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Greenhouse exception to record-keeping obligations
legislation_propositions.label: Greenhouse exception to record-keeping obligations

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Regulation 31 does not apply in a calendar year where at least 80% of the holding's agricultural area is sown with grass, the total nitrogen in organic manure applied does not exceed 100kg multiplied by the area in hectares, the total nitrogen from manufactured fertiliser does not exceed 90kg multiplied by the area in hectares, the occupier does not bring organic manure onto the holding, and the occupier records that these requirements are met.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Low-intensity farming exception to record-keeping obligations
legislation_propositions.label: Low-intensity farming exception to record-keeping obligations

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a holding who has used nitrogen fertiliser must record the yield achieved by an arable crop within one week of ascertaining it.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to record arable crop yield after nitrogen fertiliser use
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to record arable crop yield after nitrogen fertiliser use

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before 30th April each year, the occupier of a holding must record how any grassland was managed in the previous calendar year.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Annual duty to record grassland management
legislation_propositions.label: Annual duty to record grassland management

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The recording obligations in regulation 32 do not apply to crops in a greenhouse.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Greenhouse crops exemption from recording duties
legislation_propositions.label: Greenhouse crops exemption from recording duties

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An occupier of a holding who has relied on advice from a FACTS adviser for any purpose under these Regulations must keep a copy of that advice.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to retain copy of FACTS adviser advice
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to retain copy of FACTS adviser advice

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where the size of a holding changes, the occupier must update the record required by regulation 35(1) of the old Regulations or regulation 25A within one month, but only insofar as there is a change in the area of land not covered by a greenhouse.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to update holding-size record within one month when non-greenhouse land area changes
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to update holding-size record within one month when non-greenhouse land area changes

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where the amount of storage capacity of a holding changes, the occupier must update the record required by regulation 36(1)(b) of the old Regulations or regulation 25B within one week.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to update storage-capacity record within one week when capacity changes
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to update storage-capacity record within one week when capacity changes

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If the occupier introduces animals on to the holding for the first time, the occupier must within one month calculate and record the amount of manure that will be produced by the number of animals expected to be kept in a building or on hardstanding during the storage period, using the figures given in Schedule 1.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to calculate and record expected manure production within one month of first introducing animals
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to calculate and record expected manure production within one month of first introducing animals

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person required to make a record under these Regulations must keep the record for 5 years after the record ceased to be current, regardless of whether the land has ceased to be designated as a nitrate vulnerable zone.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record retention period: 5 years after record ceases to be current
legislation_propositions.label: Record retention period: 5 years after record ceases to be current

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The reference to a record required to be made under these Regulations includes a record required to be made under the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2008 in relation to which regulation 45 of those Regulations had effect immediately before commencement of these Regulations.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Transitional provision: records under 2008 Regulations included
legislation_propositions.label: Transitional provision: records under 2008 Regulations included

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Agency must determine an application for derogation as soon as practicable and notify the applicant in writing of its determination, giving reasons if the application is refused.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Determination and notification of derogation application
legislation_propositions.label: Determination and notification of derogation application

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Agency must refuse a derogation application if granting it would have an adverse effect on the integrity of a European site or European offshore marine site that has been subject to an appropriate assessment under regulation 63 of the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Mandatory refusal for adverse effect on European sites
legislation_propositions.label: Mandatory refusal for adverse effect on European sites

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Agency must refuse a derogation application if the occupier has been found in breach of the derogation conditions during the calendar year preceding that to which the application relates, subject to the exception where breach is found after application but before determination.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Mandatory refusal for prior breach of derogation conditions
legislation_propositions.label: Mandatory refusal for prior breach of derogation conditions

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person is regarded as having been found in breach of the derogation conditions if convicted of an offence under regulation 41 arising from breach of those conditions with no further appeal available or appeal decided against the person, or if the person has accepted a simple caution, had a penalty or notice imposed under regulation 42 with no further appeal or appeal decided against them, or given an enforcement undertaking under that regulation.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of 'found in breach of derogation conditions'
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of 'found in breach of derogation conditions'

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An occupier may appeal to an independent panel appointed by the Secretary of State against the Agency's refusal of an application under regulation 36.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Right to appeal refusal of derogation application
legislation_propositions.label: Right to appeal refusal of derogation application

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An appeal under regulation 38 must be submitted before the end of 30 days beginning with the day after the date of the refusal.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Time limit for submitting appeal
legislation_propositions.label: Time limit for submitting appeal

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If the panel allows an appeal under regulation 38, the Agency must designate the holding concerned as a derogated holding for the calendar year for which the application was made.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Consequence of successful appeal
legislation_propositions.label: Consequence of successful appeal

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The panel must base its decision on documents submitted by the appellant and the Agency, and such additional information from the appellant or the Agency as it considers necessary.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Basis for panel decision
legislation_propositions.label: Basis for panel decision

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Secretary of State must review the effectiveness of nitrate vulnerable zone restrictions at least every four years and revise them if necessary.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Four-yearly review and revision of NVZ restrictions
legislation_propositions.label: Four-yearly review and revision of NVZ restrictions

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Secretary of State must establish a monitoring programme to assess the effectiveness of nitrate vulnerable zone restrictions.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Monitoring programme for NVZ restrictions
legislation_propositions.label: Monitoring programme for NVZ restrictions

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: When reviewing nitrate vulnerable zone restrictions, the Secretary of State must take into account available scientific and technical data (particularly nitrogen contributions from agricultural or other sources) and regional environmental conditions.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Factors for NVZ review
legislation_propositions.label: Factors for NVZ review

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Secretary of State must ensure the public are given early and effective opportunities to participate in the review, including consultation about proposals, access to relevant information, and opportunity to express comments before decisions are made.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Public participation in NVZ review
legislation_propositions.label: Public participation in NVZ review

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Secretary of State must from time to time carry out a review of the Water Protection (Nitrate Pollution Prevention) Regulations 2015, in so far as not already done under regulation 39.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to review Regulations
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to review Regulations

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The first report under regulation 40 must be published before 31st March 2020.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Deadline for first review report
legislation_propositions.label: Deadline for first review report

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Subsequent reports under regulation 40 are to be published at intervals not exceeding 5 years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Frequency of subsequent review reports
legislation_propositions.label: Frequency of subsequent review reports

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Secretary of State must prepare a report on the implementation of these Regulations for each relevant period of four years beginning with 1st January 2016 and each successive period of four years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to prepare implementation report every four years
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to prepare implementation report every four years

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A report under regulation 40A(1) must contain details of any steps taken to promote good agricultural practice.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Report must contain details of steps to promote good agricultural practice
legislation_propositions.label: Report must contain details of steps to promote good agricultural practice

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A report under regulation 40A(1) must contain the map published under regulation 3(2), accompanied by a statement detailing the nature of, and reasons for, any revisions to the designated nitrate vulnerable zone since the end of the previous reporting period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Report must contain NVZ map with statement of revisions
legislation_propositions.label: Report must contain NVZ map with statement of revisions

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person who fails to comply with the requirements of regulations 7 and 8, regulations 10 to 13, regulations 15 to 35, or regulation 37(3) commits an offence.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Offence for non-compliance with specified regulations
legislation_propositions.label: Offence for non-compliance with specified regulations

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person guilty of an offence under regulation 41 is liable on summary conviction to a fine, or on conviction on indictment to a fine.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Penalties for offence under regulation 41
legislation_propositions.label: Penalties for offence under regulation 41

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where a body corporate commits an offence under regulation 41 with the consent, connivance or attributable neglect of a director, manager, secretary or similar officer, that person as well as the body corporate is guilty of the offence and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Corporate officer liability for body corporate offences
legislation_propositions.label: Corporate officer liability for body corporate offences

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In regulation 41(3), 'director' in relation to a body corporate whose affairs are managed by its members means a member of the body.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of 'director' for member-managed bodies corporate
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of 'director' for member-managed bodies corporate

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Agency may impose a fixed monetary penalty, variable monetary penalty, restoration notice, compliance notice or stop notice, or may accept an enforcement undertaking, in relation to an offence under regulation 41, as if it were an offence specified in Schedule 5 to the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Agency enforcement powers for regulation 41 offences
legislation_propositions.label: Agency enforcement powers for regulation 41 offences

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An expression used in paragraph (1) and in the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010 has the same meaning in that paragraph as it has in that Order.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Interpretive alignment with Environmental Civil Sanctions Order
legislation_propositions.label: Interpretive alignment with Environmental Civil Sanctions Order

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The provisions of the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010 relating to the sanctions referred to in paragraph (1) apply as if they were provisions of these Regulations.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Incorporation of Environmental Civil Sanctions Order provisions
legislation_propositions.label: Incorporation of Environmental Civil Sanctions Order provisions

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Agency has the function of enforcing these Regulations.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Agency enforcement function
legislation_propositions.label: Agency enforcement function

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2008 are revoked.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Revocation of Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2008
legislation_propositions.label: Revocation of Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2008

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Regulations 2 to 25 of the Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Amendment) and Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (England) (Amendment) Regulations 2013 are revoked.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Revocation of regulations 2–25 of 2013 Amendment Regulations on slurry and agricultural fuel oil
legislation_propositions.label: Revocation of regulations 2–25 of 2013 Amendment Regulations on slurry and agricultural fuel oil

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Amendment) Regulations 2009 are revoked.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Revocation of Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Amendment) Regulations 2009
legislation_propositions.label: Revocation of Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Amendment) Regulations 2009

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Amendment) Regulations 2012 are revoked.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Revocation of Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Amendment) Regulations 2012
legislation_propositions.label: Revocation of Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Amendment) Regulations 2012

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A dairy cow after first calf with an annual milk yield more than 9000 litres produces 64 litres of manure, 315 grams of nitrogen, and 142 grams of phosphate daily.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Daily manure, nitrogen and phosphate production by high-yield dairy cow
legislation_propositions.label: Daily manure, nitrogen and phosphate production by high-yield dairy cow
legislation_propositions.fragment_locator: Schedule 1, Grazing livestock table, Cattle – Dairy cow – After first calf and annual milk yield more than 9000 litres

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A sow including litter up to 7kg fed on a diet supplemented with synthetic amino acids produces 10.9 litres of manure, 44 grams of nitrogen, and 37 grams of phosphate daily.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Daily manure, nitrogen and phosphate production by sow with litter (amino acid-supplemented diet)
legislation_propositions.label: Daily manure, nitrogen and phosphate production by sow with litter (amino acid-supplemented diet)
legislation_propositions.fragment_locator: Schedule 1, Non-grazing livestock table, Pigs – sow (including litter up to 7kg) fed on a diet supplemented with synthetic amino acids

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A sow including litter up to 7kg fed on a diet without synthetic amino acids produces 10.9 litres of manure, 49 grams of nitrogen, and 37 grams of phosphate daily.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Daily manure, nitrogen and phosphate production by sow with litter (non-supplemented diet)
legislation_propositions.label: Daily manure, nitrogen and phosphate production by sow with litter (non-supplemented diet)
legislation_propositions.fragment_locator: Schedule 1, Non-grazing livestock table, Pigs – sow (including litter up to 7kg) fed on a diet without synthetic amino acids

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Figures for a ewe include one or more suckled lambs until the lambs are aged 6 months.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Ewe manure figures include suckled lambs up to 6 months
legislation_propositions.label: Ewe manure figures include suckled lambs up to 6 months

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry from cattle contains 2.6 kg of total nitrogen per cubic metre.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Nitrogen content in cattle slurry
legislation_propositions.label: Nitrogen content in cattle slurry

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: At least five samples, each of two litres, must be taken in the case of slurry and other liquid and semi-liquid organic manure.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry sampling requirement - number and volume
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry sampling requirement - number and volume
legislation_propositions.fragment_locator: Schedule 2, Part 2, Slurry and other liquid and semi-liquid organic manure, paragraph 1

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry or other manure must, if it is reasonably practicable to do so, be thoroughly mixed before the samples are taken; and each sample must be taken from a different location.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry sampling - mixing and location requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry sampling - mixing and location requirements
legislation_propositions.fragment_locator: Schedule 2, Part 2, Slurry and other liquid and semi-liquid organic manure, paragraph 2

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Dirty water contains 0.5 kg of total nitrogen per cubic metre.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Nitrogen content in dirty water
legislation_propositions.label: Nitrogen content in dirty water

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In the case of slurry and other liquid and semi-liquid organic manure, at least five samples, each of two litres, must be taken.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum sampling requirement for slurry and liquid/semi-liquid organic manure
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum sampling requirement for slurry and liquid/semi-liquid organic manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The slurry or other manure must, if it is reasonably practicable to do so, be thoroughly mixed before the samples are taken; and each sample must be taken from a different location.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Mixing and location requirements for slurry sampling
legislation_propositions.label: Mixing and location requirements for slurry sampling

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Each sample must be taken from a vessel; but if a tanker used for spreading is fitted with a suitable valve, the samples may be taken while spreading and each sample must be taken at intervals during the spreading.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Vessel sampling requirement with tanker exception for slurry
legislation_propositions.label: Vessel sampling requirement with tanker exception for slurry

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Each sample must be poured into a larger container, stirred thoroughly and a two-litre sample taken from that container and poured into a smaller, clean container, and the two-litre sample must then be sent for analysis.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Sample preparation and submission procedure for slurry
legislation_propositions.label: Sample preparation and submission procedure for slurry

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Solid manure samples must be taken from a manure heap.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Solid manure sampling location
legislation_propositions.label: Solid manure sampling location

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: At least ten samples of 1kg each must be taken from different locations in a manure heap, each at least 0.5 metres from the surface.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Solid manure sampling quantity and depth
legislation_propositions.label: Solid manure sampling quantity and depth

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Solid manure samples must be placed on a clean, dry tray or sheet, lumps broken up, thoroughly mixed together, and a representative sample of at least 2kg sent for analysis.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Solid manure sample preparation and submission
legislation_propositions.label: Solid manure sample preparation and submission

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For calculating compliance with the whole farm limit for pigs and poultry, four samples for analysis must be taken in a calendar year (one per quarter) from manure heaps not more than 12 months old.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Whole farm limit sampling frequency for pigs and poultry
legislation_propositions.label: Whole farm limit sampling frequency for pigs and poultry

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a derogated holding must ensure that the area of the holding in hectares is greater than or equal to the total nitrogen in livestock manure from grazing livestock divided by 250 plus the total nitrogen in livestock manure from non-grazing livestock divided by 170, for the calendar year for which the derogation has effect.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Limit on application of livestock manure nitrogen
legislation_propositions.label: Limit on application of livestock manure nitrogen

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a derogated holding must maintain the holding to ensure at least 80% of the agricultural area is sown with grass during the calendar year to which the derogation applies.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum grassland requirement for derogated holdings
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum grassland requirement for derogated holdings

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where livestock manure has been spread on grass on sandy soils on a derogated holding between 1st September and 31st December, the grass must not be ploughed before the following 16th January.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Closed period for ploughing grass on sandy soils after manure spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Closed period for ploughing grass on sandy soils after manure spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In Schedule 3, "the occupier" means the occupier of a derogated holding.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of "the occupier" in Schedule 3
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of "the occupier" in Schedule 3

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In Schedule 3, "the holding" means the derogated holding.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of "the holding" in Schedule 3
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of "the holding" in Schedule 3

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must ensure that in the calendar year for which the derogation has effect, the area of the derogated holding (A) is greater than or equal to the sum of (i) the total nitrogen from grazing livestock manure divided by 250, and (ii) the total nitrogen from non-grazing livestock manure divided by 170.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Derogation area requirement based on nitrogen from livestock manure
legislation_propositions.label: Derogation area requirement based on nitrogen from livestock manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For the purposes of the derogation area formula, 'A' means the area of the derogated holding in hectares as at 1st January in the calendar year for which the derogation has effect.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of 'A' (area) in derogation formula
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of 'A' (area) in derogation formula

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For the purposes of the derogation area formula, 'Ngl' means the total amount of nitrogen in kilogrammes in livestock manure from animals listed as 'grazing livestock' in Schedule 1, whether applied directly by an animal or by spreading.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of 'Ngl' (nitrogen from grazing livestock) in derogation formula
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of 'Ngl' (nitrogen from grazing livestock) in derogation formula

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For the purposes of the derogation area formula, 'Nngl' means the total amount of nitrogen in kilogrammes in livestock manure from animals listed as 'non-grazing livestock' in Schedule 1, whether applied directly by an animal or by spreading.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of 'Nngl' (nitrogen from non-grazing livestock) in derogation formula
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of 'Nngl' (nitrogen from non-grazing livestock) in derogation formula

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the amount of phosphorus in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop during the growing season.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Calculation of available soil phosphorus
legislation_propositions.label: Calculation of available soil phosphorus

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of phosphorus available in the soil.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Calculation of optimum phosphate fertiliser amount
legislation_propositions.label: Calculation of optimum phosphate fertiliser amount

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must produce a plan for the spreading of phosphate fertiliser for that growing season.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Production of phosphate fertiliser spreading plan
legislation_propositions.label: Production of phosphate fertiliser spreading plan

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In the case of permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the phosphate fertiliser planning duties in each calendar year before spreading phosphate fertiliser.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Timing of compliance for permanent grassland
legislation_propositions.label: Timing of compliance for permanent grassland

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The fertilisation plan for the holding must include a sketch plan indicating the location of the fields to which the plan relates and clearly state the nature of the fertilizer to be used in any field referred to in the plan.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fertilisation plan: sketch and fertilizer nature requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Fertilisation plan: sketch and fertilizer nature requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The fertilisation plan must record the amount of phosphorus calculated under paragraph 3(1)(a), the method used to calculate that figure, and the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop taking into account the calculated phosphorus amount.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fertilisation plan: phosphorus calculation and optimum phosphate recording
legislation_propositions.label: Fertilisation plan: phosphorus calculation and optimum phosphate recording

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The fertilisation plan must record the amount of nitrogen likely to be available for uptake by the crop from any organic manure intended to be spread for crop uptake in the growing season during the calendar year in which it is spread, and the amount of phosphate likely to be supplied to meet the requirement of the crop from any organic manure spread or intended to be spread during the calendar year.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fertilisation plan: organic manure nitrogen and phosphate availability recording
legislation_propositions.label: Fertilisation plan: organic manure nitrogen and phosphate availability recording

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The fertilisation plan must record the amount of manufactured nitrogen fertiliser required (being the optimum amount of nitrogen required by the crop less the amount of nitrogen that will be available for crop uptake from any organic manure spread during that calendar year) and the amount of manufactured phosphate fertiliser required (being the optimum amount of phosphate required by the crop less the amount of phosphate supplied for crop uptake from any organic manure spread for the purpose of fertilising the crop during that calendar year).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fertilisation plan: manufactured fertiliser requirement calculation recording
legislation_propositions.label: Fertilisation plan: manufactured fertiliser requirement calculation recording

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier of a derogated holding must undertake soil sampling and analysis for phosphorus supply at least every four years for at least every five hectares of the agricultural area under the same cropping regime and soil type.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Phosphorus soil sampling obligation (four-year cycle)
legislation_propositions.label: Phosphorus soil sampling obligation (four-year cycle)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier may rely on previous phosphorus soil sampling and analysis results if the sampling was carried out within four years before the grant of the derogation.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Reliance on previous phosphorus sampling
legislation_propositions.label: Reliance on previous phosphorus sampling
