legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser (kg) that should be spread on the crop during the relevant period, taking into account the soil phosphorus index, within the period beginning with 1 January 2024 and ending with 30 March 2024.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Calculation of optimum phosphate fertiliser amount
legislation_propositions.label: Calculation of optimum phosphate fertiliser amount

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An enhanced nutrient management plan for a holding must include a risk map produced in accordance with paragraph 11(1) indicating the location of the fields to which the plan relates, and must clearly state the type of fertiliser to be used in relation to any field referred to in the plan.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Enhanced nutrient management plan: risk map and fertiliser type requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Enhanced nutrient management plan: risk map and fertiliser type requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An enhanced nutrient management plan must record the soil phosphorus index for each area of the holding with the same cropping regime, nutrient management regime and soil type.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Enhanced nutrient management plan: soil phosphorus index recording
legislation_propositions.label: Enhanced nutrient management plan: soil phosphorus index recording

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An enhanced nutrient management plan must record the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser (kg) that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the soil phosphorus index.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Enhanced nutrient management plan: optimum phosphate fertiliser recording
legislation_propositions.label: Enhanced nutrient management plan: optimum phosphate fertiliser recording

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An enhanced nutrient management plan must record the amount of nitrogen (kg) likely to be available for uptake by the crop from any organic manure intended to be spread for crop uptake in the growing season during the relevant period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Enhanced nutrient management plan: nitrogen from organic manure recording
legislation_propositions.label: Enhanced nutrient management plan: nitrogen from organic manure recording

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must ensure that the total amount of phosphate from manufactured phosphate fertiliser and phosphate from organic manure spread in the growing season does not exceed the limits set out in paragraph 9 during the relevant period, irrespective of the figure recorded in the enhanced nutrient management plan.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Total phosphate application limit (manufactured and organic)
legislation_propositions.label: Total phosphate application limit (manufactured and organic)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Subject to sub-paragraph (2), the total amount of phosphate spread on any crop listed in the tables must not exceed the figure under the applicable soil phosphorus index number in the same table.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Maximum phosphate application limits by crop and soil phosphorus index
legislation_propositions.label: Maximum phosphate application limits by crop and soil phosphorus index

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: At P Index 4 and 5, up to 60 kg P₂O₅/ha can be used as a starter fertiliser close to the seed, provided the amount applied as a starter dose together with the amount added in the base dressing does not exceed the amount of phosphate required to replace that removed by the previous crop.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Starter fertiliser exception for P Index 4 and 5
legislation_propositions.label: Starter fertiliser exception for P Index 4 and 5

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Spreading phosphate on grass and other crops above the values stipulated within the tables is permitted subject to prior receipt of written advice from a person who is a member of the Fertiliser Advisers Certification and Training Scheme.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for exceeding table limits with FACTS advice
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for exceeding table limits with FACTS advice

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before spreading organic manure during the relevant period, the occupier must record the total phosphate content (kg) of the organic manure.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Recording phosphate content of organic manure before spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Recording phosphate content of organic manure before spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser during the relevant period, the occupier must record the amount of phosphate (kg) required, being the optimum amount required by the crop less the amount supplied from any organic manure spread.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Recording required phosphate amount for manufactured fertiliser
legislation_propositions.label: Recording required phosphate amount for manufactured fertiliser

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Before spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser during the relevant period, the occupier must record the planned month for spreading.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Recording planned month for manufactured phosphate fertiliser spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Recording planned month for manufactured phosphate fertiliser spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In addition to the requirements under regulation 11 (risk maps), the risk map must show each field marked with a reference number or number to enable cross reference to fields recorded in fertilisation plans.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Risk map must show fields with reference numbers for cross-reference to fertilisation plans
legislation_propositions.label: Risk map must show fields with reference numbers for cross-reference to fertilisation plans

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The risk map must correspond with the agricultural area of the holding.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Risk map must correspond with agricultural area of holding
legislation_propositions.label: Risk map must correspond with agricultural area of holding

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The risk map must be completed by 31 March 2024.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Risk map completion deadline: 31 March 2024
legislation_propositions.label: Risk map completion deadline: 31 March 2024

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where a change in circumstances affects a matter referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b), the occupier must update the map within one month of the change, beginning with the day after the change.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Occupier must update risk map within one month of relevant change
legislation_propositions.label: Occupier must update risk map within one month of relevant change

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must maintain the holding to ensure at least 80% of the agricultural area is sown with grass during the relevant period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum grass cover requirement for agricultural holdings
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum grass cover requirement for agricultural holdings

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must ensure that no person ploughs temporary grassland on sandy soils on the holding within the period beginning with 1 July 2024 and ending with 31 December 2024.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on ploughing temporary grassland on sandy soils (1 July–31 December 2024)
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on ploughing temporary grassland on sandy soils (1 July–31 December 2024)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must ensure that no person ploughs grass on sandy soils before 16 January 2024 on the holding where livestock manure has been spread on that grass within the period beginning with 1 September and ending with 31 December in the previous calendar year.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on ploughing manured grass on sandy soils before 16 January 2024
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on ploughing manured grass on sandy soils before 16 January 2024

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must ensure that no person ploughs grass on soils that are not sandy soils on the holding before 16 January 2024 where livestock manure has been spread on that grass within the period beginning with 15 October in the previous calendar year and ending with 15 January 2024.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on ploughing manured grass on non-sandy soils before 16 January 2024
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on ploughing manured grass on non-sandy soils before 16 January 2024

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where grass on a holding is ploughed during the relevant period, the land must be sown with a crop with high nitrogen demand within four weeks beginning with the day after the date of ploughing grass.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Ploughed grass land – sowing with high nitrogen demand crop
legislation_propositions.label: Ploughed grass land – sowing with high nitrogen demand crop

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Crop rotation on the holding during the relevant period must not include leguminous or other plants fixing atmospheric nitrogen, except for grass with less than 50% clover or any other leguminous plants that are under-sown with grass.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on leguminous crops in rotation with exceptions
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on leguminous crops in rotation with exceptions

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must record the total agricultural area and the area of grass within the holding by 1 March 2024.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to record agricultural area and grass area by 1 March 2024
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to record agricultural area and grass area by 1 March 2024

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If the size of the holding or area of grass within it changes, the occupier must update the record within one month beginning with the day after the change.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to update record within one month of change in holding or grass area
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to update record within one month of change in holding or grass area

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must record the expected number and category of livestock to be kept on the holding during the relevant period, in accordance with the categories in Tables 1 and 2 in Schedule 1.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record expected livestock numbers and categories
legislation_propositions.label: Record expected livestock numbers and categories

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Following the record of expected livestock numbers, the occupier must calculate and record the amount of nitrogen and phosphate (kg) in manure expected to be produced by the livestock on the holding during the relevant period using Tables 1 and 2 in Schedule 1.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Calculate and record expected nitrogen and phosphate in manure
legislation_propositions.label: Calculate and record expected nitrogen and phosphate in manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The records required under sub-paragraphs (1) and (2) must be made before 1 March 2024.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Deadline for livestock and manure nutrient records
legislation_propositions.label: Deadline for livestock and manure nutrient records

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must make a record of the type and amount of livestock manure (tonnes or cubic metres as applicable) that is intended to be sent off the holding during the relevant period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record type and amount of livestock manure intended to be sent off holding
legislation_propositions.label: Record type and amount of livestock manure intended to be sent off holding

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must assess and record the amount of nitrogen (kg) in the livestock manure recorded under paragraph (a) in accordance with regulation 36(4) and Parts 1 and 2 of Schedule 3.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Assess and record nitrogen content in livestock manure to be sent off holding
legislation_propositions.label: Assess and record nitrogen content in livestock manure to be sent off holding

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The records to be made under sub-paragraph (1) must be made by 1 March 2024.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Deadline for livestock manure records
legislation_propositions.label: Deadline for livestock manure records

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If the occupier intends to spread phosphate fertiliser during the relevant period, the occupier must within one week of sowing a crop record the crop sown and the date of sowing, in addition to the requirements of regulation 39.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record-keeping for phosphate fertiliser spreading: crop and sowing date
legislation_propositions.label: Record-keeping for phosphate fertiliser spreading: crop and sowing date

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must, during the relevant period, record within one week of spreading organic manure the total phosphorus content (kg).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record phosphorus content of organic manure within one week
legislation_propositions.label: Record phosphorus content of organic manure within one week

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The recording requirements in paragraph 20 are in addition to the requirements of regulation 40 (records of spreading nitrogen fertiliser).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Paragraph 20 requirements are additional to regulation 40
legislation_propositions.label: Paragraph 20 requirements are additional to regulation 40

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must record the date of ploughing grass on the holding within one week of that ploughing during the relevant period, in addition to the requirements of regulation 41 (subsequent records).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Record date of ploughing grass within one week
legislation_propositions.label: Record date of ploughing grass within one week

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier, or any person on behalf of the occupier, must submit fertilisation accounts for the relevant period to NRW by 31 March 2025 by e-mail.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to submit fertilisation accounts to NRW by 31 March 2025
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to submit fertilisation accounts to NRW by 31 March 2025

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The fertilisation account must record the total agricultural area of the holding in hectares and the area of the holding in hectares covered by specified crop types including winter wheat, spring wheat, winter barley, spring barley, winter oilseed rape, sugar beet, potatoes, forage maize, grass, and other crops.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fertilisation account must record agricultural area and crop coverage
legislation_propositions.label: Fertilisation account must record agricultural area and crop coverage

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The fertilisation account must record the number and category of animals kept on the holding during the relevant period in accordance with the categories described in Tables 1 and 2 in Schedule 1, and the amount of nitrogen and phosphate (kg) in the manure produced by those animals calculated using Tables 1 and 2 in Schedule 1.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fertilisation account must record livestock numbers and manure nutrient content
legislation_propositions.label: Fertilisation account must record livestock numbers and manure nutrient content

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The fertilisation account must record the weight (tonnes) and nitrogen content (kg) of all manufactured nitrogen fertiliser stocks kept on the holding, brought on to and sent off the holding during the relevant period, and the weight (tonnes) and phosphate content (kg) of all manufactured phosphate fertiliser stocks kept on the holding, brought on to and sent off the holding during the relevant period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fertilisation account must record manufactured fertiliser stocks and movements
legislation_propositions.label: Fertilisation account must record manufactured fertiliser stocks and movements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must protect all soil by ensuring that all land is covered by crops, stubbles, residues or other vegetation at all times, except where establishing such cover would create a significant risk of soil erosion and significant risk of nitrogen and phosphorus getting into surface water.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Soil protection through continuous vegetation cover
legislation_propositions.label: Soil protection through continuous vegetation cover

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where land has been harvested using a combine harvester, forage harvester or mower, the occupier must ensure that the stubble of the harvested crop remains in the land at all times throughout the relevant period beginning with the first day after harvest and ending with 31 December 2024.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Stubble retention after harvest (option a)
legislation_propositions.label: Stubble retention after harvest (option a)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where land has been harvested using a combine harvester, forage harvester or mower, the occupier must ensure that the land is prepared as a seedbed for a crop or temporary cover crop within 14 days of harvest, beginning with the first day after harvest, and the crop or temporary cover crop is sown within a period of 10 days beginning with the day after final seedbed preparation.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Seedbed preparation and sowing timescales (option b(i))
legislation_propositions.label: Seedbed preparation and sowing timescales (option b(i))

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where sowing within the 10-day period would lead to significant risk of soil erosion and nitrogen or phosphorus entering a surface water, the crop or temporary cover crop must be sown as soon as is practicable after the land ceases to be waterlogged.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Deferred sowing when erosion risk exists (option b(ii))
legislation_propositions.label: Deferred sowing when erosion risk exists (option b(ii))

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must ensure that sites where supplementary feeding for livestock are provided are not located within 20 metres of a watercourse on any land during the relevant period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Livestock supplementary feeding sites: 20-metre watercourse buffer
legislation_propositions.label: Livestock supplementary feeding sites: 20-metre watercourse buffer

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The occupier must ensure that sites where supplementary drinking for livestock are provided are not located within 10 metres of a watercourse on any land during the relevant period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Livestock supplementary drinking sites: 10-metre watercourse buffer
legislation_propositions.label: Livestock supplementary drinking sites: 10-metre watercourse buffer

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An occupier who intends to spread slurry on the holding during the relevant period must use precision spreading equipment.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Mandatory use of precision spreading equipment for slurry spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Mandatory use of precision spreading equipment for slurry spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: During the relevant period, no person may spread organic manure within 15 metres of surface water unless using precision spreading equipment.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on spreading organic manure within 15 metres of surface water (general)
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on spreading organic manure within 15 metres of surface water (general)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: When using precision spreading equipment during the relevant period, no person may spread organic manure within 10 metres of surface water.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on spreading organic manure within 10 metres of surface water (precision equipment)
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on spreading organic manure within 10 metres of surface water (precision equipment)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry and other liquid and semi-liquid organic manure must be sampled by taking at least five samples, each of 2 litres.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum sample number and volume for liquid organic manure
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum sample number and volume for liquid organic manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If a tanker used for spreading is fitted with a suitable valve, slurry samples may be taken while spreading, and each sample must be taken at intervals during the spreading.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Alternative tanker sampling method for slurry
legislation_propositions.label: Alternative tanker sampling method for slurry

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In relation to slurry and other liquid and semi-liquid organic manure, at least five samples, each of 2 litres, must be taken.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum sampling requirement for slurry and liquid/semi-liquid organic manure
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum sampling requirement for slurry and liquid/semi-liquid organic manure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Subject to sub-paragraph (3), the five samples must be taken from a vessel, with the slurry thoroughly mixed before sampling if reasonably practicable, and each sample must be taken from a different location.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Vessel sampling procedure for slurry samples
legislation_propositions.label: Vessel sampling procedure for slurry samples

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If a tanker used for spreading is fitted with a suitable valve, the samples may be taken while spreading, and each sample must be taken at intervals during the spreading.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Alternative tanker sampling procedure during spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Alternative tanker sampling procedure during spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The five samples must be poured into a larger container, stirred thoroughly, and a 2 litre sample must be taken from that container and poured into a smaller clean container, then sent for analysis.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Composite sample preparation and submission for analysis
legislation_propositions.label: Composite sample preparation and submission for analysis

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Samples of solid manures must be taken from a manure heap.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Solid manure sampling location
legislation_propositions.label: Solid manure sampling location

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: At least ten samples of 1 kg each must be taken from solid manure, each from a different location in a heap, with each sub-sample taken at least 0.5 metres from the surface of the heap.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Solid manure sampling quantity and depth
legislation_propositions.label: Solid manure sampling quantity and depth

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: When calculating compliance with the whole farm limit for pigs and poultry, four samples for analysis must be taken in a calendar year (one in each quarter) from manure heaps not more than 12 months old.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Quarterly sampling for pig and poultry whole farm limit compliance
legislation_propositions.label: Quarterly sampling for pig and poultry whole farm limit compliance

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Sub-samples of solid manure must be placed on a clean, dry tray or sheet, any lumps broken up and thoroughly mixed together, and a representative sample of at least 2 kg sent for analysis.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Solid manure sample preparation and submission
legislation_propositions.label: Solid manure sample preparation and submission

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Nitrogen must not be spread on permitted crops after 31 October.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on nitrogen spreading after 31 October
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on nitrogen spreading after 31 October

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An additional 50 kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread every four weeks during the closed period up to the end of harvest.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Additional nitrogen spreading allowance during closed period
legislation_propositions.label: Additional nitrogen spreading allowance during closed period

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A maximum of 40 kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread at any one time.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Maximum single application rate for nitrogen
legislation_propositions.label: Maximum single application rate for nitrogen

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Oilseed rape (winter) has a maximum nitrogen rate of 30 kg per hectare during the closed period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Nitrogen limit for winter oilseed rape
legislation_propositions.label: Nitrogen limit for winter oilseed rape
legislation_propositions.fragment_locator: Schedule 4, crop table row: Oilseed rape, winter

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of the silo, its effluent tank and channels and the walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for silo infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for silo infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of the silo, its effluent tank or channels or any pipes may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which silage effluent could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum separation distance from waterbodies
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum separation distance from waterbodies

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A silo must comply with the provisions of Schedule 5 in order to satisfy the requirement.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo compliance requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo compliance requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo must extend beyond any walls of the silo.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo base extension requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo base extension requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo must be provided at its perimeter with channels designed and constructed so as to collect any silage effluent that escapes from the silo.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo perimeter channel requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo perimeter channel requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo must have adequate provision for the drainage of silage effluent from perimeter channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo effluent drainage provision requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo effluent drainage provision requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The capacity of the effluent tank must not be less than 20 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity where the silo has a capacity of less than 1,500 cubic metres.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effluent tank minimum capacity for silos < 1,500 m³
legislation_propositions.label: Effluent tank minimum capacity for silos < 1,500 m³

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The capacity of the effluent tank must not be less than 30 cubic metres plus 6.7 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity in excess of 1,500 cubic metres where the silo has a capacity of 1,500 cubic metres or more.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effluent tank minimum capacity for silos ≥ 1,500 m³
legislation_propositions.label: Effluent tank minimum capacity for silos ≥ 1,500 m³

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo must be designed in accordance with BS 8007:1987 (code of practice for design of concrete structures for retaining aqueous liquids) or constructed using appropriate hot-rolled asphalt in accordance with BS 5502: Part 21:1990 (code of practice for selection and use of construction materials).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo base design and construction standards
legislation_propositions.label: Silo base design and construction standards

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of the silo, the base and walls of its effluent tank and channels, and walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for silo and effluent infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for silo and effluent infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of a silo, its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes must, so far as reasonably practicable, be resistant to attack by silage effluent.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silage infrastructure must be resistant to silage effluent attack
legislation_propositions.label: Silage infrastructure must be resistant to silage effluent attack

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of a silo, its effluent tank, channels, or pipes may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which silage effluent could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo and effluent infrastructure: 10-metre separation from waters
legislation_propositions.label: Silo and effluent infrastructure: 10-metre separation from waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Retaining walls of a silo must be capable of withstanding minimum wall loadings calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraph 15.6 of BS 5502: Part 22: 2003.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo retaining wall loading capacity requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo retaining wall loading capacity requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A silo with retaining walls must at no time be loaded to a depth exceeding the maximum depth consistent with the design assumption made in respect of the loadings of the retaining walls.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo maximum loading depth restriction
legislation_propositions.label: Silo maximum loading depth restriction

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Notices must be displayed on the retaining walls of a silo in accordance with paragraph 18 of BS 5502: Part 22: 2003.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo retaining wall notice display requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo retaining wall notice display requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A silo, its effluent tank and channels and any pipes must be designed and constructed so that with proper maintenance they are likely to continue to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 5 and, if applicable, paragraph 7(a) for at least 20 years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Design and construction durability requirement for silos and effluent infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Design and construction durability requirement for silos and effluent infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An effluent tank with any part below ground level must be designed and constructed to satisfy structural and impermeability requirements for at least 20 years without maintenance.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Below-ground effluent tank: 20-year design life without maintenance
legislation_propositions.label: Below-ground effluent tank: 20-year design life without maintenance

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a slurry storage tank, the base and walls of any effluent tank, channels and reception pit, and the walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for slurry storage system components
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for slurry storage system components

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of the slurry storage tank, any effluent tank, channels and reception pit, and the walls of any pipes must be protected against corrosion in accordance with paragraph 7 of BS 5502: Part 50: 1993.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Corrosion protection requirement for slurry storage system components
legislation_propositions.label: Corrosion protection requirement for slurry storage system components

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of the slurry storage tank or any effluent tank, channels or reception pit may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which slurry could enter if it were to escape, unless precautions are taken that NRW agrees in writing are adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum distance requirement from waters for slurry storage systems
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum distance requirement from waters for slurry storage systems

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage system must satisfy specified requirements.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry storage system requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry storage system requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a slurry storage tank must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement: slurry storage tank base
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement: slurry storage tank base

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of any effluent tank, channels and reception pit must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement: effluent tank, channels, reception pit
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement: effluent tank, channels, reception pit
legislation_propositions.fragment_locator: schedule 6, paragraph 2 (effluent tank, channels, reception pit)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement: pipe walls
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement: pipe walls

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of slurry storage tanks, effluent tanks, channels, reception pits, and the walls of pipes must be protected against corrosion in accordance with BS 5502: Part 50: 1993, paragraph 7.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Corrosion protection for slurry and effluent storage infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Corrosion protection for slurry and effluent storage infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of a slurry storage tank and of any reception pit must be capable of withstanding characteristic loads calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraph 5 of BS 5502: Part 50: 1993.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Structural load-bearing requirements for slurry storage tanks and reception pits
legislation_propositions.label: Structural load-bearing requirements for slurry storage tanks and reception pits

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Facilities used for the temporary storage of slurry before transfer to a slurry storage tank must have adequate capacity to store the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced on the premises in any two day period (disregarding slurry transferred directly into a slurry storage tank).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Temporary slurry storage capacity requirement (two-day maximum)
legislation_propositions.label: Temporary slurry storage capacity requirement (two-day maximum)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Facilities used for the temporary storage of slurry before transfer to a slurry storage tank may have a lesser capacity than the two-day maximum if NRW agrees in writing that the lesser capacity is adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Temporary slurry storage capacity exception (NRW agreement)
legislation_propositions.label: Temporary slurry storage capacity exception (NRW agreement)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where slurry flows into a channel before discharging into a reception pit and the flow of slurry out of the channel is controlled by means of a sluice, the capacity of the reception pit must be adequate to hold the maximum quantity of slurry that can be released by opening the sluice.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Reception pit capacity requirement (sluice-controlled channel)
legislation_propositions.label: Reception pit capacity requirement (sluice-controlled channel)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage tank with walls made of earth must have at least 750 mm of freeboard.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Freeboard requirement for earth-walled slurry storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Freeboard requirement for earth-walled slurry storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage tank (other than one with walls made of earth) must have at least 300 mm of freeboard.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Freeboard requirement for non-earth-walled slurry storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Freeboard requirement for non-earth-walled slurry storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, channels, or reception pit may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which slurry could enter if it were to escape, unless precautions agreed in writing by NRW are taken that are adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: 10-metre separation distance for slurry storage from waters (or NRW-agreed precautions)
legislation_propositions.label: 10-metre separation distance for slurry storage from waters (or NRW-agreed precautions)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage tank and any effluent tank, channels, pipes and reception pit must be designed and constructed so that with proper maintenance they are likely to continue to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 4 for at least 20 years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Design and construction durability requirement for slurry storage and effluent infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Design and construction durability requirement for slurry storage and effluent infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank must extend beyond the walls.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Base extension requirement for non-impermeable slurry tank walls
legislation_propositions.label: Base extension requirement for non-impermeable slurry tank walls

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage tank, effluent tank, or reception pit fitted with a drainage pipe must have two valves in series on the pipe, each valve separated from the other by a minimum distance of 1 metre, subject to exceptions.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Two-valve requirement for drainage pipes on slurry/effluent tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Two-valve requirement for drainage pipes on slurry/effluent tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Each valve on a drainage pipe of a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, or reception pit must be capable of shutting off the flow of slurry through the pipe and must be kept shut and locked in that position when not in use.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Valve capability and operational requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Valve capability and operational requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The two-valve requirement does not apply to a slurry storage tank that drains through the pipe into another slurry storage tank if the other tank is of equal or greater capacity.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception: equal or greater capacity receiving tank
legislation_propositions.label: Exception: equal or greater capacity receiving tank

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The two-valve requirement does not apply to a slurry storage tank that drains through the pipe into another slurry storage tank if the tops of the tanks are at the same level.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception: same-level tank tops
legislation_propositions.label: Exception: same-level tank tops

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations may be cited as the Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (England) Regulations 2010.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Citation
legislation_propositions.label: Citation

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations apply to England only.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Territorial extent
legislation_propositions.label: Territorial extent

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations come into force on 6th April 2010.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Commencement
legislation_propositions.label: Commencement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry is defined as liquid or semi-liquid matter composed of excreta produced by livestock while in a yard or building (including that held in wood chip corrals), or a mixture wholly or mainly consisting of livestock excreta, livestock bedding, rainwater and washings from a building or yard used by livestock, of a consistency that allows it to be pumped or discharged by gravity at any stage in the handling process.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of slurry
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of slurry

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage system includes a slurry storage tank and any reception pit and any effluent tank used in connection with the tank, and any channels and pipes used in connection with the tank, any reception pit or any effluent tank.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Components of slurry storage system
legislation_propositions.label: Components of slurry storage system

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Silage effluent means effluent from silage.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of silage effluent
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of silage effluent

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A requirement for a silo or slurry storage tank to conform to a British Standard is satisfied if the silo or tank conforms to a standard or specification that provides an equivalent level of protection and performance.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Equivalence to British Standard for slurry storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Equivalence to British Standard for slurry storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person with custody or control of silage being made or stored must keep it in a silo satisfying Schedule 1 requirements, or compress it into bales wrapped in impermeable membranes and stored at least 10 metres from inland freshwaters or coastal waters, or (for field silage on open land) give the Agency 14 days' notice and ensure the place is at least 10 metres from inland freshwaters or coastal waters and at least 50 metres from the nearest relevant abstraction point of any protected water supply source.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silage storage requirements: silo, baled, or field silage conditions
legislation_propositions.label: Silage storage requirements: silo, baled, or field silage conditions

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A water supply source is a protected water supply source if any relevant water abstraction from the source is licensed under Part II of the Water Resources Act 1991, or the person making or storing the silage was aware of the source's location before the making of the silage began or (if the silage was made elsewhere) before it was stored on the land in question.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of protected water supply source for silage storage
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of protected water supply source for silage storage

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person who has custody or control of a silage bale must not open or remove the wrapping of the bale within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters which silage effluent could enter as a result.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on opening silage bale wrapping near waters
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on opening silage bale wrapping near waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For the purposes of silage storage requirements, 'relevant water abstraction' means the abstraction of water for use for human consumption, or domestic purposes (other than human consumption), or manufacturing food or drink for human consumption; and 'water supply source' means inland freshwaters or ground waters from which a relevant abstraction is made or licensed to be made.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definitions of relevant water abstraction and water supply source
legislation_propositions.label: Definitions of relevant water abstraction and water supply source

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person having custody or control of slurry must store it only in a slurry storage system that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 2.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry storage system requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry storage system requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The requirement to store slurry in a compliant slurry storage system does not apply to slurry while it is stored temporarily in a tanker that is used for transporting slurry on roads or about a farm.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for temporary storage in transport tankers
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for temporary storage in transport tankers

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person who has custody or control of fuel oil on a farm must ensure that it is stored in a fuel storage tank within a storage area or facility that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 3, in drums within such a storage area, or in an underground fuel storage tank, subject to exceptions.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fuel oil storage requirements on farms
legislation_propositions.label: Fuel oil storage requirements on farms

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The fuel oil storage requirements do not apply to the temporary storage of fuel oil in a tanker used for transporting fuel oil on roads or about a farm.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for temporary storage in transport tankers
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for temporary storage in transport tankers

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The fuel oil storage requirements do not apply where the total quantity of fuel oil stored on the farm does not exceed 1,500 litres.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for small quantities under 1,500 litres
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for small quantities under 1,500 litres

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations do not apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank which, before 1st March 1991, was being used for the purpose of making silage, storing slurry or storing fuel oil.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exemption for pre-1991 operational slurry storage systems
legislation_propositions.label: Exemption for pre-1991 operational slurry storage systems

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations do not apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank which was constructed before 1st March 1991 for the purpose of making silage, storing slurry or storing fuel oil, even if not used before that date.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exemption for pre-1991 constructed but unused slurry storage systems
legislation_propositions.label: Exemption for pre-1991 constructed but unused slurry storage systems

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations do not apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank where a contract for its construction, substantial enlargement or substantial reconstruction was entered into before 1st March 1991 and the work was completed before 1st September 1991.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exemption for slurry storage systems contracted before March 1991 and completed before September 1991
legislation_propositions.label: Exemption for slurry storage systems contracted before March 1991 and completed before September 1991

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank otherwise exempt under paragraph (1) if any requirement of a notice under regulation 7 is not complied with within the period stated in the notice.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Loss of exemption for non-compliance with enforcement notice
legislation_propositions.label: Loss of exemption for non-compliance with enforcement notice

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person served with a regulation 7 notice may appeal to the Secretary of State within 28 days beginning on the day after the date on which the notice is served, or such longer period as the Secretary of State allows.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Right to appeal regulation 7 notice within 28 days
legislation_propositions.label: Right to appeal regulation 7 notice within 28 days

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An appeal under regulation 8 must be made by the appellant serving notice on the Secretary of State, and the notice must contain or be accompanied by a statement of the grounds of appeal.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Appeal procedure requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Appeal procedure requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: On determining an appeal under regulation 8, the Secretary of State may direct the Agency to withdraw the regulation 7 notice, modify any of its requirements, extend the period for compliance with any requirement, or dismiss the appeal.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Secretary of State's powers on determining appeal
legislation_propositions.label: Secretary of State's powers on determining appeal

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The period for compliance with a regulation 7 notice against which an appeal has been made is extended so that it expires on the date on which the Secretary of State finally determines the appeal or, if the appeal is withdrawn, the date on which it is withdrawn, subject to any direction under paragraph (5).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Automatic extension of compliance period during appeal
legislation_propositions.label: Automatic extension of compliance period during appeal

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Regulation 9 applies to any silo, slurry or fuel oil storage system whose construction is to be begun on or after 15 June 2013.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Application to new or improved stores (post-15 June 2013)
legislation_propositions.label: Application to new or improved stores (post-15 June 2013)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person who proposes to have custody or control of silage, slurry or fuel oil in a new or improved store must give the Agency notice specifying the type of silo or storage system and its location at least 14 days before construction work begins.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Notice requirement for new or improved stores
legislation_propositions.label: Notice requirement for new or improved stores

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For the purposes of regulation 9, 'construction' includes substantial enlargement and reconstruction.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of 'construction' for new or improved stores
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of 'construction' for new or improved stores

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person who contravenes regulation 9 is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 2 on the standard scale.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Offence and penalty for contravention of regulation 9
legislation_propositions.label: Offence and penalty for contravention of regulation 9

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) Regulations 1991 are revoked in so far as they relate to England.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Revocation of 1991 Regulations (England)
legislation_propositions.label: Revocation of 1991 Regulations (England)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (Amendment) Regulations 1997 are revoked in so far as they relate to England.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Revocation of 1997 Amendment Regulations (England)
legislation_propositions.label: Revocation of 1997 Amendment Regulations (England)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo must extend beyond any walls of the silo, be provided at its perimeter with channels designed and constructed to collect any silage effluent that escapes from the silo, and have adequate provision for the drainage of that effluent from those channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo base construction and drainage requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Silo base construction and drainage requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The capacity of the effluent tank must not be less than 20 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity in the case of a silo with a capacity of less than 1,500 cubic metres.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effluent tank capacity for silos under 1,500 cubic metres
legislation_propositions.label: Effluent tank capacity for silos under 1,500 cubic metres

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The capacity of the effluent tank must not be less than 30 cubic metres plus 6.7 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity in excess of 1,500 cubic metres in the case of a silo with a capacity of 1,500 cubic metres or more.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effluent tank capacity for silos of 1,500 cubic metres or more
legislation_propositions.label: Effluent tank capacity for silos of 1,500 cubic metres or more

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of the silo, its effluent tank or channels or any pipes may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which silage effluent could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum separation distance from waters
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum separation distance from waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A silo must comply with the provisions of Schedule 1 in order to satisfy the requirement.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo compliance requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo compliance requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo must extend beyond any walls of the silo.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo base extension requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo base extension requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo must be provided at its perimeter with channels designed and constructed so as to collect any silage effluent that escapes from the silo.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo perimeter channel requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo perimeter channel requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo must have adequate provision for the drainage of silage effluent from perimeter channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo effluent drainage requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo effluent drainage requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The capacity of the effluent tank for a silo with a capacity of less than 1,500 cubic metres must not be less than 20 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effluent tank capacity requirement for silos < 1,500 m³
legislation_propositions.label: Effluent tank capacity requirement for silos < 1,500 m³

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The capacity of the effluent tank for a silo with a capacity of 1,500 cubic metres or more must not be less than 30 cubic metres plus 6.7 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity in excess of 1,500 cubic metres.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effluent tank capacity requirement for silos ≥ 1,500 m³
legislation_propositions.label: Effluent tank capacity requirement for silos ≥ 1,500 m³

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo must be designed in accordance with BS 8007:1987 (code of practice for design of concrete structures for retaining aqueous liquids) or constructed using appropriate hot-rolled asphalt in accordance with BS 5502:Part 21:1990 (code of practice for selection and use of construction materials).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo base design standards
legislation_propositions.label: Silo base design standards

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of the silo, the base and walls of its effluent tank and channels, and walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for silo and effluent infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for silo and effluent infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of a silo, its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes must, so far as reasonably practicable, be resistant to attack by silage effluent.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Resistance to silage effluent attack
legislation_propositions.label: Resistance to silage effluent attack

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of a silo, its effluent tank, channels, or pipes may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which silage effluent could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: 10-metre separation distance for silos and effluent infrastructure from inland freshwaters and coastal waters
legislation_propositions.label: 10-metre separation distance for silos and effluent infrastructure from inland freshwaters and coastal waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Retaining walls of a silo must be capable of withstanding minimum wall loadings calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraphs 15.6 of BS 5502: Part 22:2003.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo retaining wall loading capacity requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo retaining wall loading capacity requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A silo must at no time be loaded to a depth exceeding the maximum depth consistent with the design assumption made in respect of the loadings of the retaining walls.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo maximum loading depth restriction
legislation_propositions.label: Silo maximum loading depth restriction

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Notices must be displayed on the retaining walls of a silo in accordance with paragraph 18 of BS 5502: Part 22:2003.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo retaining wall notice display requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Silo retaining wall notice display requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A silo, its effluent tank and channels and any pipes must be designed and constructed so that with proper maintenance they are likely to continue to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 5 and, if applicable, paragraph 7(a) for at least 20 years, subject to paragraph 9.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo and effluent infrastructure: 20-year design and construction durability standard
legislation_propositions.label: Silo and effluent infrastructure: 20-year design and construction durability standard

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An effluent tank with any part below ground level must be designed and constructed to satisfy structural and impermeability requirements for at least 20 years without maintenance.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Below-ground effluent tank: 20-year design life without maintenance
legislation_propositions.label: Below-ground effluent tank: 20-year design life without maintenance

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a slurry storage tank, the base and walls of any effluent tank, channels and reception pit, and the walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for slurry storage system components
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for slurry storage system components

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of the slurry storage tank, any effluent tank, channels and reception pit, and the walls of any pipes must be protected against corrosion in accordance with paragraph 7 of BS 5502: Part 50:1993.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Corrosion protection requirement for slurry storage system components
legislation_propositions.label: Corrosion protection requirement for slurry storage system components

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where slurry is proposed to be utilised on the premises by spreading it on the land, the slurry storage tank need not have a greater storage capacity than is adequate to hold the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced in any four month period, taking into account specified matters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Four-month storage capacity sufficiency for land-spreading utilisation
legislation_propositions.label: Four-month storage capacity sufficiency for land-spreading utilisation

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of the slurry storage tank or any effluent tank, channels or reception pit may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which slurry could enter if it were to escape, unless the Agency agrees in writing that precautions are adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: 10-metre setback from waters or Agency-approved precautions
legislation_propositions.label: 10-metre setback from waters or Agency-approved precautions

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage system must satisfy specified requirements.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry storage system requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry storage system requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a slurry storage tank must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement: slurry storage tank base
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement: slurry storage tank base

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of any effluent tank must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement: effluent tank base and walls
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement: effluent tank base and walls

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Channels and reception pits must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement: channels and reception pits
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement: channels and reception pits

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement: pipe walls
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement: pipe walls

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of slurry storage tanks, effluent tanks, channels, reception pits, and the walls of pipes must be protected against corrosion in accordance with BS 5502: Part 50:1993, paragraph 7.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Corrosion protection for slurry and effluent storage infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Corrosion protection for slurry and effluent storage infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of a slurry storage tank and of any reception pit must be capable of withstanding characteristic loads calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraph 5 of BS 5502: Part 50: 1993.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Structural load-bearing requirements for slurry storage tanks and reception pits
legislation_propositions.label: Structural load-bearing requirements for slurry storage tanks and reception pits

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Facilities used for the temporary storage of slurry before transfer to a slurry storage tank must have adequate capacity to store the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced on the premises in any two day period (disregarding slurry transferred directly into a slurry storage tank).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Temporary slurry storage capacity requirement (two-day maximum)
legislation_propositions.label: Temporary slurry storage capacity requirement (two-day maximum)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Facilities used for the temporary storage of slurry before transfer to a slurry storage tank may have a lesser capacity than the two-day maximum if the Agency agrees in writing that the lesser capacity is adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Temporary slurry storage capacity exception (Agency agreement)
legislation_propositions.label: Temporary slurry storage capacity exception (Agency agreement)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where slurry flows into a channel before discharging into a reception pit and the flow of slurry out of the channel is controlled by a sluice, the capacity of the reception pit must be adequate to hold the maximum quantity of slurry that can be released by opening the sluice.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Reception pit capacity requirement (sluice-controlled channel)
legislation_propositions.label: Reception pit capacity requirement (sluice-controlled channel)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage tank must have adequate storage capacity for the likely quantities of slurry produced from time to time on the premises, taking into account the proposed method of utilising the slurry and the likely rates and times of utilisation, and the matters specified in sub-paragraph (3).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Adequate storage capacity requirement for slurry storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Adequate storage capacity requirement for slurry storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where slurry is to be utilised on the premises by spreading it on the land, the tank need not have a greater storage capacity than is adequate to hold the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced in any four month period, taking into account the matters mentioned in sub-paragraph (3).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Four-month storage capacity exception for on-site land spreading
legislation_propositions.label: Four-month storage capacity exception for on-site land spreading

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In determining adequate storage capacity under sub-paragraphs (1) and (2), account must be taken of the storage capacity of any other slurry storage tank on the premises.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Consideration of other slurry storage tanks on premises
legislation_propositions.label: Consideration of other slurry storage tanks on premises

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In determining adequate storage capacity under sub-paragraphs (1) and (2), account must be taken of the need to provide at least 750 millimetres of freeboard in the case of a tank with walls made of earth and 300 millimetres of freeboard in all other cases.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Freeboard requirements for slurry storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Freeboard requirements for slurry storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, channels, or reception pit may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which slurry could enter if it were to escape, unless precautions agreed in writing by the Agency are taken that are adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: 10-metre separation distance for slurry storage from waters (unless Agency-agreed precautions)
legislation_propositions.label: 10-metre separation distance for slurry storage from waters (unless Agency-agreed precautions)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage tank and any effluent tank, channels, pipes and reception pit must be designed and constructed so that with proper maintenance they are likely to continue to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 4 for at least 20 years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Design and construction durability requirement for slurry storage and effluent infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Design and construction durability requirement for slurry storage and effluent infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank must extend beyond the walls.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Base extension requirement for non-impermeable slurry tank walls
legislation_propositions.label: Base extension requirement for non-impermeable slurry tank walls

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: If a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, or reception pit is fitted with a drainage pipe, there must be two valves in series on the pipe with each valve separated from the other by a minimum distance of 1 metre, subject to the exception for tanks draining into equal or greater capacity tanks.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Two-valve requirement for drainage pipes on slurry/effluent tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Two-valve requirement for drainage pipes on slurry/effluent tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Each valve on a drainage pipe of a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, or reception pit must be capable of shutting off the flow of slurry through the pipe.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Valve capability requirement for slurry drainage systems
legislation_propositions.label: Valve capability requirement for slurry drainage systems

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Each valve on a drainage pipe of a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, or reception pit must be kept shut and locked in that position when not in use.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Valve shut-and-locked requirement when not in use
legislation_propositions.label: Valve shut-and-locked requirement when not in use

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The two-valve requirement does not apply to a slurry storage tank that drains through the pipe into another slurry storage tank if the other tank is of equal or greater capacity or if the tops of the tanks are at the same level.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception to two-valve requirement for inter-tank drainage
legislation_propositions.label: Exception to two-valve requirement for inter-tank drainage

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage tank with walls made of earth must not be filled to a level that allows less than 750 millimetres of freeboard.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum freeboard for earth-walled slurry storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum freeboard for earth-walled slurry storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A fuel oil storage area with a single fuel storage tank and no other fuel oil stored must be surrounded by a bund capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than 110 per cent of the capacity of the tank.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Bund capacity requirement for single-tank fuel oil storage area
legislation_propositions.label: Bund capacity requirement for single-tank fuel oil storage area

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The bund and the base of a fuel oil storage area must be impermeable to water and oil and designed and constructed so that with proper maintenance they are likely to remain so for at least 20 years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability and durability requirements for fuel oil storage bund and base
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability and durability requirements for fuel oil storage bund and base

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel storage tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be within the bund, arranged to discharge vertically downwards, and shut and locked when not in use.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Requirements for taps and valves on fuel storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Requirements for taps and valves on fuel storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of the fuel storage area or the bund enclosing it may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters that fuel oil could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum separation distance from waters for fuel oil storage area
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum separation distance from waters for fuel oil storage area

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Requirements must be satisfied in relation to a fuel oil storage area.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fuel oil storage area requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Fuel oil storage area requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where a storage area contains only one fuel storage tank and fuel oil is not otherwise stored there, the bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than 110 per cent of the capacity of that tank.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Bund capacity: single tank (110%)
legislation_propositions.label: Bund capacity: single tank (110%)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where a storage area contains more than one fuel storage tank and fuel oil is not otherwise stored there, the bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than the greater of (i) 110 per cent of the capacity of the largest tank or (ii) 25 per cent of the total volume of oil that could be stored in the tanks.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Bund capacity: multiple tanks (110% largest or 25% total)
legislation_propositions.label: Bund capacity: multiple tanks (110% largest or 25% total)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where a storage area contains no fuel storage tank, the bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than 25 per cent of the total volume of oil at any time stored within the area.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Bund capacity: no tank (25% of stored volume)
legislation_propositions.label: Bund capacity: no tank (25% of stored volume)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In any other case, the bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than the greatest of (i) 110 per cent of the capacity of the largest tank, (ii) if more than one tank, 25 per cent of the total volume that could be stored in the tanks, or (iii) 25 per cent of the total volume of oil at any time stored within the area.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Bund capacity: other cases (110% largest, 25% tank total, or 25% stored)
legislation_propositions.label: Bund capacity: other cases (110% largest, 25% tank total, or 25% stored)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The bund and the base of the area must be impermeable to water and oil.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for bund and base
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for bund and base

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The bund and the base of the area must be designed and constructed so that they are of sufficient strength and structural integrity so that with proper maintenance they are likely to remain so for at least 20 years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Structural integrity and durability requirement for bund and base
legislation_propositions.label: Structural integrity and durability requirement for bund and base

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Every part of any fuel storage tank must be within the bund.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fuel storage tank bund containment requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Fuel storage tank bund containment requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel storage tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be within the bund.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Tap/valve location requirement (within bund)
legislation_propositions.label: Tap/valve location requirement (within bund)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A flexible pipe permanently attached to a fuel tank through which fuel is delivered must be fitted with a tap or valve at its end that closes automatically when not in use.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Automatic closure tap/valve requirement for permanently attached flexible fuel delivery pipe
legislation_propositions.label: Automatic closure tap/valve requirement for permanently attached flexible fuel delivery pipe

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of the fuel storage area or the bund enclosing it may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters that fuel oil could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum 10-metre separation distance for fuel storage from waters
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum 10-metre separation distance for fuel storage from waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations may be cited as the Reduction and Prevention of Agricultural Diffuse Pollution (England) Regulations 2018.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Citation
legislation_propositions.label: Citation
