legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations come into force on 2nd April 2018.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Commencement date
legislation_propositions.label: Commencement date

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations extend to England and Wales.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Territorial extent
legislation_propositions.label: Territorial extent

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations apply to agricultural land in England.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Territorial application
legislation_propositions.label: Territorial application

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must not apply organic manure or manufactured fertiliser to agricultural land if the soil is waterlogged, flooded or snow covered.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on applying manure/fertiliser to waterlogged, flooded or snow covered soil
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on applying manure/fertiliser to waterlogged, flooded or snow covered soil

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must ensure that each application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser to agricultural land is planned so that it does not exceed the needs of the soil and crop on that land or give rise to a significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Planning requirement for organic manure and manufactured fertiliser applications
legislation_propositions.label: Planning requirement for organic manure and manufactured fertiliser applications

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must ensure that each application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser to agricultural land takes into account the weather conditions and forecasts for that land at the time of the application.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Weather conditions consideration requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Weather conditions consideration requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: When planning to avoid significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution, a land manager must ensure that factors including slope of the land (particularly if greater than 12 degrees), ground cover, proximity to inland freshwaters, coastal waters, wetlands, or to a spring, well or borehole, soil type and condition, and presence and condition of agricultural land drains are taken into account.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Risk factors to be considered in planning
legislation_propositions.label: Risk factors to be considered in planning

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In addition to planning requirements, a land manager must ensure that reasonable precautions are taken to prevent agricultural diffuse pollution resulting from applications of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser.
legislation_propositions.short_name: General reasonable precautions duty
legislation_propositions.label: General reasonable precautions duty

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: When planning an application of organic manure or fertiliser to cultivated agricultural land, a land manager must ensure that the results of soil sampling and analysis are taken into account.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to consider soil sampling results when planning applications to cultivated land
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to consider soil sampling results when planning applications to cultivated land

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Soil sampling and analysis results must include the pH of the soil and the levels of nitrogen, phosphorous, magnesium and potassium present, must be no more than 5 years old at the time of application, and may have been collected before these Regulations came into force or by another land manager.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Requirements for soil sampling and analysis results
legislation_propositions.label: Requirements for soil sampling and analysis results

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Nitrogen levels may be determined by means of assessment of the soil nitrogen supply, rather than by sampling and analysis of soil.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Alternative method for determining nitrogen levels
legislation_propositions.label: Alternative method for determining nitrogen levels

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Cultivated agricultural land means agricultural land which has been cultivated by physical means (including ploughing, sowing or harvesting) at least once in the previous year, or by chemical means (including the application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser) at least once in the previous 3 years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of cultivated agricultural land
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of cultivated agricultural land

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must ensure that manufactured fertiliser is not applied to agricultural land within two metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters, or of a spring, well or borehole.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on applying manufactured fertiliser within two metres of water bodies
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on applying manufactured fertiliser within two metres of water bodies

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must not apply organic manure to agricultural land within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Organic manure: 10-metre buffer zone from waters
legislation_propositions.label: Organic manure: 10-metre buffer zone from waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where precision spreading equipment is used, organic manure must not be applied within 6 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Precision spreading: 6-metre buffer zone
legislation_propositions.label: Precision spreading: 6-metre buffer zone

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure) may be applied to land managed for breeding wader birds or species-rich semi-natural grassland subject to agri-environmental commitment or SSSI notification, during 1 June to 31 October, provided it is not applied directly onto waters and does not exceed 12.5 tonnes per hectare annually.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Livestock manure exception: breeding wader / semi-natural grassland
legislation_propositions.label: Livestock manure exception: breeding wader / semi-natural grassland

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: "Agri-environmental commitment" means any commitment entered into under Council Regulation (EC) No. 1698/2005 or Regulation (EU) No. 1305/2013 on support for rural development by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition: agri-environmental commitment
legislation_propositions.label: Definition: agri-environmental commitment

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must ensure that organic manure is not applied to agricultural land within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on applying organic manure within 50 metres of water sources
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on applying organic manure within 50 metres of water sources

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must not store organic manure on agricultural land within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on storing organic manure within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on storing organic manure within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must not store organic manure on agricultural land within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on storing organic manure within 50 metres of springs, wells or boreholes
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on storing organic manure within 50 metres of springs, wells or boreholes

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For agricultural land not subject to the distance restrictions in regulation 9(1), a land manager must take into account any factors creating a significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution when deciding where to store organic manure.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Risk assessment requirement for organic manure storage on other agricultural land
legislation_propositions.label: Risk assessment requirement for organic manure storage on other agricultural land

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The factors to be considered under regulation 9(2) include those specified in regulation 4(2).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Cross-reference to factors in regulation 4(2) for organic manure storage risk assessment
legislation_propositions.label: Cross-reference to factors in regulation 4(2) for organic manure storage risk assessment

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must prevent poaching within 5 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition of poaching near water bodies
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition of poaching near water bodies

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must not position a livestock feeder within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Livestock feeder setback from water bodies
legislation_propositions.label: Livestock feeder setback from water bodies

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must not position a livestock feeder within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Livestock feeder setback from groundwater sources
legislation_propositions.label: Livestock feeder setback from groundwater sources

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must take reasonable precautions to prevent agricultural diffuse pollution resulting from land management and cultivation practices on agricultural land.
legislation_propositions.short_name: General duty to prevent diffuse pollution from land practices
legislation_propositions.label: General duty to prevent diffuse pollution from land practices

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person who fails to comply with the requirements of any of regulations 3 to 10 commits an offence.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Offence for non-compliance with regulations 3 to 10
legislation_propositions.label: Offence for non-compliance with regulations 3 to 10

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person guilty of an offence under regulation 11 is liable, either on summary conviction or on conviction on indictment, to a fine.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Penalty for offence under regulation 11
legislation_propositions.label: Penalty for offence under regulation 11

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where a body corporate is guilty of an offence under regulation 11 and the offence is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of an officer, or to have been attributable to any neglect on the part of an officer, the officer as well as the body corporate is guilty of the offence and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Officer liability for corporate offences
legislation_propositions.label: Officer liability for corporate offences

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In regulation 11(3), 'officer' means a director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of the body, or a person purporting to act in any such capacity.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of 'officer' for corporate liability
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of 'officer' for corporate liability

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For an offence under regulation 11(1), the Agency may impose a restoration notice, compliance notice, stop notice, fixed monetary penalty, variable monetary penalty or accept an enforcement undertaking as if it were an offence specified in Schedule 5 to the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Agency enforcement powers for regulation 11(1) offences
legislation_propositions.label: Agency enforcement powers for regulation 11(1) offences

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An expression used in regulation 13(1) and in the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010 has the same meaning in regulation 13(1) as it has in that Order.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Interpretive alignment with Environmental Civil Sanctions Order
legislation_propositions.label: Interpretive alignment with Environmental Civil Sanctions Order

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The provisions of the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010 relating to the sanctions in regulation 13(1) apply as if they were provisions of these Regulations.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Incorporation of Environmental Civil Sanctions Order provisions
legislation_propositions.label: Incorporation of Environmental Civil Sanctions Order provisions

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Agency has the function of enforcing these Regulations.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Agency enforcement function
legislation_propositions.label: Agency enforcement function

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Secretary of State may issue guidance to the Agency with respect to the exercise of the Agency's functions under these Regulations.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Power to issue guidance to Agency
legislation_propositions.label: Power to issue guidance to Agency

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In the exercise of its functions, the Agency must have regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State under regulation 15(1).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Agency duty to have regard to guidance
legislation_propositions.label: Agency duty to have regard to guidance

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Secretary of State must publish any guidance issued under regulation 15(1) on a website maintained by or on behalf of the Secretary of State.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Duty to publish guidance on website
legislation_propositions.label: Duty to publish guidance on website

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations may be cited as the Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (Scotland) Regulations 2003 and shall come into force on 1st December 2003.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Citation and commencement
legislation_propositions.label: Citation and commencement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry means excreta, including any liquid fraction, produced by livestock whilst in a yard or building; or a mixture consisting wholly of or containing such excreta, bedding, feed residues, rainwater and washings from a building or yard used by livestock, dungsteads or middens, high level slatted buildings and weeping wall structures or any combination of these, provided such excreta is present, of a consistency that allows it to be pumped or discharged by gravity at any stage in the handling process.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of slurry
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of slurry

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry storage system means a slurry storage tank; any reception pit and any effluent tank used in connection with the slurry storage tank; and any channels and pipes used in connection with the slurry storage tank, any reception pit or any effluent tank.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Definition of slurry storage system
legislation_propositions.label: Definition of slurry storage system

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: These Regulations shall extend to Scotland only.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Territorial extent
legislation_propositions.label: Territorial extent

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person having custody or control of a crop being made into silage or of silage being stored must keep it in a silo that satisfies Schedule 1 requirements or is an exempt structure under regulation 5.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silage storage in compliant or exempt silo
legislation_propositions.label: Silage storage in compliant or exempt silo

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person having custody or control of silage made in the form of wrapped and sealed bales must not open or remove the wrapping unless done at a place at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Prohibition on opening wrapped silage bales near waters
legislation_propositions.label: Prohibition on opening wrapped silage bales near waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person having custody or control of slurry must store it in a slurry storage system that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 2 or is an exempt structure by virtue of regulation 5.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry storage system requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry storage system requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The slurry storage system requirement does not apply to slurry while it is stored temporarily in a tanker with a capacity not exceeding 18,000 litres which is used for transporting slurry on roads or about a farm.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception for temporary storage in transport tankers
legislation_propositions.label: Exception for temporary storage in transport tankers

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No person shall have custody or control of fuel oil on a farm unless it is stored in a fuel storage tank or container within a storage area that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 3.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fuel oil storage in compliant tank/container
legislation_propositions.label: Fuel oil storage in compliant tank/container

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Fuel oil on a farm may be stored in drums within a storage area that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 3.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fuel oil storage in drums
legislation_propositions.label: Fuel oil storage in drums

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Fuel oil on a farm may be stored temporarily in a tanker used for transporting fuel oil on roads or about the farm.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Temporary fuel oil storage in tanker
legislation_propositions.label: Temporary fuel oil storage in tanker

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The prohibition on fuel oil storage does not apply if the total quantity of fuel oil stored on the farm does not exceed 1,250 litres.
legislation_propositions.short_name: De minimis exemption for fuel oil storage
legislation_propositions.label: De minimis exemption for fuel oil storage

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A silo, slurry storage system, fuel storage tank or container is an exempt structure if it was an exempt structure under the 2001 Regulations and had not ceased to be exempt immediately before these Regulations came into force, and it does not cease to be exempt by virtue of regulation 7(1).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Transitional exemption for structures exempt under 2001 Regulations
legislation_propositions.label: Transitional exemption for structures exempt under 2001 Regulations

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Regulation 2 does not apply where a person makes bulk bagged silage on a farm in bags that are made of 1000 gauge polyethylene or material of at least equivalent impermeability and durability, are kept sealed to prevent the escape of silage effluent, and are stored on a firm level surface and incorporate a facility designed to enable the safe removal of excess effluent when present.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exemption from regulation 2 for bulk bagged silage meeting specified standards
legislation_propositions.label: Exemption from regulation 2 for bulk bagged silage meeting specified standards

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person is not entitled to rely on the exemption for bulk bagged silage unless that person stores any bags in which silage is being made or stored at a place at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: 10-metre distance requirement for bulk bagged silage storage
legislation_propositions.label: 10-metre distance requirement for bulk bagged silage storage

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No person having custody or control of any crop which has been made into silage in bulk bags shall open or empty any bag in which silage has been made unless that person does so at a place at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: 10-metre distance requirement for opening or emptying bulk bagged silage
legislation_propositions.label: 10-metre distance requirement for opening or emptying bulk bagged silage

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An exempt structure shall cease to be exempt if any requirement of a notice under regulation 8(1) is not complied with within the period stated in the notice.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Loss of exemption for non-compliance with notice
legislation_propositions.label: Loss of exemption for non-compliance with notice

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: References to the period stated in a notice include that period as extended under regulation 8(5) or by virtue of regulation 9(5) or (6), and references to a requirement of a notice include that requirement as modified under regulation 8(5) or by virtue of regulation 9(5).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Interpretation of notice periods and requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Interpretation of notice periods and requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: SEPA may serve notice on any person with custody or control of any relevant substance requiring that person to carry out works, take precautions, or take other steps to reduce to a minimum any significant risk of pollution of inland or coastal waters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: SEPA power to serve notice requiring pollution prevention measures
legislation_propositions.label: SEPA power to serve notice requiring pollution prevention measures

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A notice served under regulation 8 must specify or describe the required works, precautions or steps, state the compliance period, and inform the recipient of the effect of regulation 9.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Mandatory content of SEPA notice
legislation_propositions.label: Mandatory content of SEPA notice

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The works, precautions or steps specified in a notice may include the requirement to establish and implement a Farm Waste Management Plan in accordance with the code of practice approved under section 51(1) of the Control of Pollution Act 1974.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Notice may require Farm Waste Management Plan
legislation_propositions.label: Notice may require Farm Waste Management Plan

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The compliance period stated in a notice must be reasonable in the circumstances and must not end earlier than 28 days from the day the notice is served.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum 28-day compliance period for notice
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum 28-day compliance period for notice

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person served with a notice under regulation 8 may appeal to the Scottish Ministers within 28 days beginning with the day on which that notice is served, or within such longer period as the Scottish Ministers may allow.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Right to appeal regulation 8 notice within 28 days
legislation_propositions.label: Right to appeal regulation 8 notice within 28 days

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: An appeal under regulation 9 shall be made by the appellant serving notice on the Scottish Ministers, and the notice shall contain or be accompanied by a statement of the grounds of appeal.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Appeal procedure requires notice with grounds of appeal
legislation_propositions.label: Appeal procedure requires notice with grounds of appeal

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: On determining an appeal under regulation 9, the Scottish Ministers may direct SEPA to withdraw the notice, extend the period for compliance with any requirement of the notice, modify any requirement of the notice, or dismiss the appeal.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Scottish Ministers' powers on determining appeal
legislation_propositions.label: Scottish Ministers' powers on determining appeal

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The period for compliance with a notice under regulation 8 shall be extended so that it expires on the date on which the Scottish Ministers finally determine the appeal or, if the appeal is withdrawn, the date on which it is withdrawn.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Automatic extension of compliance period pending appeal determination
legislation_propositions.label: Automatic extension of compliance period pending appeal determination

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person who proposes to have custody or control of any relevant substance which is to be kept or stored on a farm in a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage area constructed, substantially enlarged or substantially reconstructed on or after 29th December 2003 shall serve notice on SEPA specifying the type of structure to be used and its location at least 28 days before it is to be used for such purpose.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Notice to SEPA for new or substantially altered storage structures
legislation_propositions.label: Notice to SEPA for new or substantially altered storage structures

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A person who contravenes regulation 2(1), 2(2), 3(1), 4(1), 6 or 10 commits an offence.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Offence for contravention of specified regulations
legislation_propositions.label: Offence for contravention of specified regulations

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: On summary conviction for contravening regulation 2(1), 2(2), 3(1), 4(1), 6 or 10, a person is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months or to a fine not exceeding £20,000 or to both.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Penalty on summary conviction
legislation_propositions.label: Penalty on summary conviction

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: On conviction on indictment for contravening regulation 2(1), 2(2), 3(1), 4(1), 6 or 10, a person is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years or to a fine or to both.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Penalty on conviction on indictment
legislation_propositions.label: Penalty on conviction on indictment

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (Scotland) Regulations 1999 (insofar as they remain in force) and the 2001 Regulations are revoked.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Revocation of 1999 and 2001 Regulations
legislation_propositions.label: Revocation of 1999 and 2001 Regulations

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo with retaining walls made other than of earth must extend beyond those walls, and in all cases the base must be provided with channels constructed to collect any silage effluent which may escape from the silo, with adequate provision for drainage of that effluent from the channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo base construction and effluent collection requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Silo base construction and effluent collection requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For a silo with capacity less than 1500 cubic metres, the effluent tank capacity must be not less than 3 cubic metres for each 150 cubic metres or part thereof of silo capacity.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effluent tank capacity for silos under 1500 cubic metres
legislation_propositions.label: Effluent tank capacity for silos under 1500 cubic metres

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For a silo with capacity of 1500 cubic metres or more, the effluent tank capacity must be not less than 30 cubic metres plus 1 cubic metre for each 150 cubic metres or part thereof of silo capacity in excess of 1500 cubic metres.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effluent tank capacity for silos of 1500 cubic metres or more
legislation_propositions.label: Effluent tank capacity for silos of 1500 cubic metres or more

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of the silo, its effluent tank, channels, or any associated pipes may be situated within 10 metres of any inland or coastal waters which silage effluent could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum separation distance from waters
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum separation distance from waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A silo must comply with the provisions of this Schedule or be designed and constructed in accordance with BS 5502 (parts relating to Cylindrical Forage Towers).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo compliance requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Silo compliance requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where a silo has retaining walls made other than of earth, the base of the silo shall extend beyond those walls.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo base extension requirement (non-earth walls)
legislation_propositions.label: Silo base extension requirement (non-earth walls)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of the silo shall in all cases be provided with channels so constructed as to collect any silage effluent which may escape from the silo.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Silo base channels for effluent collection
legislation_propositions.label: Silo base channels for effluent collection

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Adequate provision shall be made for the drainage of silage effluent from the channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Drainage provision from channels to effluent tank
legislation_propositions.label: Drainage provision from channels to effluent tank

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For a silo with a capacity of less than 1500 cubic metres, the effluent tank capacity shall be not less than 3 cubic metres for each 150 cubic metres or part thereof of silo capacity.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effluent tank capacity for silos < 1500 m³
legislation_propositions.label: Effluent tank capacity for silos < 1500 m³

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: For a silo with a capacity of 1500 cubic metres or more, the effluent tank capacity shall be not less than 30 cubic metres plus 1 cubic metre for each 150 cubic metres or part thereof of silo capacity in excess of 1500 cubic metres.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Effluent tank capacity for silos ≥ 1500 m³
legislation_propositions.label: Effluent tank capacity for silos ≥ 1500 m³

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The effluent collection system associated with silos may, with the agreement of SEPA, incorporate a system of pumps and sumps, together with detailed sizing, pumping and management requirements, designed to reduce the capacity of the effluent tank.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Alternative effluent system with SEPA agreement
legislation_propositions.label: Alternative effluent system with SEPA agreement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a silo, the base and walls of its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for silo bases, effluent tanks, channels and pipes
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for silo bases, effluent tanks, channels and pipes

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and any walls of the silo, its effluent tank and channels and the walls of any pipes shall, so far as reasonably practicable, be resistant to attack by silage effluent.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Resistance to silage effluent attack
legislation_propositions.label: Resistance to silage effluent attack

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where the walls of the silo, effluent tank, channels or pipes are made of earth, they shall be lined with an impermeable membrane.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeable membrane lining for earth walls
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeable membrane lining for earth walls

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of a silage silo, its effluent tank, channels, or any associated pipes shall be situated within 10 metres of any inland or coastal waters which silage effluent could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum 10-metre separation distance for silage infrastructure from waters
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum 10-metre separation distance for silage infrastructure from waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Retaining walls of a silo must be capable of withstanding minimum wall loadings calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraph 15.6.1 to 15.6.3 of BS 5502 (Part 22: 1993).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Retaining wall strength requirement for silos
legislation_propositions.label: Retaining wall strength requirement for silos

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A silo with retaining walls must not at any time be loaded to a depth exceeding the maximum depth consistent with the design assumption made in respect of the loadings of the retaining walls.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Maximum loading depth restriction for silos with retaining walls
legislation_propositions.label: Maximum loading depth restriction for silos with retaining walls

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A silo, its effluent tank and channels and any pipes must be designed and constructed so that with proper maintenance they are likely to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 5 and, if applicable, 7(a) for a period of at least 20 years, subject to paragraph 9.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Design and construction durability requirement for silos and effluent infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Design and construction durability requirement for silos and effluent infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Any part of an effluent tank installed below ground level shall be designed and constructed in accordance with BS 5502 so that with proper maintenance it is likely to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5 for a period of at least 20 years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Below-ground effluent tank design and construction standard
legislation_propositions.label: Below-ground effluent tank design and construction standard

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a slurry storage tank, the base and walls of any effluent tank, channels and reception pit, and the walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for slurry storage system components
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for slurry storage system components

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of slurry storage tanks, effluent tanks, channels, reception pits, and pipe walls must be protected against corrosion in accordance with paragraph 7.2 of BS 5502 (Part 50: 1993).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Corrosion protection requirement for slurry storage system components
legislation_propositions.label: Corrosion protection requirement for slurry storage system components

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, channels, pipes, or reception pit may be situated within 10 metres of any inland or coastal waters which slurry could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum separation distance from waters for slurry storage systems
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum separation distance from waters for slurry storage systems

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, or reception pit is fitted with a drainage pipe, there must be two valves in series on the pipe, each capable of stopping slurry flow and kept shut and locked when not in use, unless the tank drains into another slurry storage tank of equal or greater capacity or where the tops of the tanks are at the same level.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Dual valve requirement for drainage pipes on slurry storage systems
legislation_propositions.label: Dual valve requirement for drainage pipes on slurry storage systems

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage system must satisfy specified requirements.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Slurry storage system requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Slurry storage system requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a slurry storage tank shall be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for slurry storage tank base
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for slurry storage tank base

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of any effluent tank, channels and reception pit shall be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for effluent tank, channels and reception pit
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for effluent tank, channels and reception pit

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The walls of any pipes used for slurry or effluent shall be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for pipe walls
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for pipe walls

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of slurry storage tanks, effluent tanks, channels, reception pits, and the walls of pipes must be protected against corrosion in accordance with paragraph 7.2 of BS 5502 (Part 50: 1993).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Corrosion protection requirement for slurry and effluent storage infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Corrosion protection requirement for slurry and effluent storage infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The base and walls of a slurry storage tank and any reception pit must be capable of withstanding characteristic loads calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraph 5 of the Code of Practice.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Structural capacity requirement for slurry storage tank and reception pit
legislation_propositions.label: Structural capacity requirement for slurry storage tank and reception pit

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Facilities used for the temporary storage of slurry before transfer to a slurry storage tank must have adequate capacity to store the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced on a farm in any two day period.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Temporary slurry storage capacity requirement (two-day rule)
legislation_propositions.label: Temporary slurry storage capacity requirement (two-day rule)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where slurry flows into a channel before discharging into a reception pit and the flow is controlled by a sluice, the capacity of the reception pit must be adequate to store the maximum quantity of slurry which can be released by opening the sluice.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Reception pit capacity requirement for sluice-controlled channels
legislation_propositions.label: Reception pit capacity requirement for sluice-controlled channels

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage tank must have adequate storage capacity for the likely quantities of slurry produced from time to time on the farm, having regard to the proposed method of disposal (including likely rates and times of disposal) and specified matters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Adequate slurry storage capacity requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Adequate slurry storage capacity requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where slurry is to be disposed of on a farm by spreading it on the land, the tank need not have a greater storage capacity than is adequate to store the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced in any continuous six month period, having regard to specified matters.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Six-month storage capacity limit for land-spreading disposal
legislation_propositions.label: Six-month storage capacity limit for land-spreading disposal

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In determining adequate slurry storage capacity, regard must be had to the storage capacity of any other slurry storage tank on the premises.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Consideration of other slurry storage tanks on premises
legislation_propositions.label: Consideration of other slurry storage tanks on premises

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: In determining adequate slurry storage capacity, regard must be had to the need to provide not less than 750 millimetres of freeboard for tanks with earth walls and 300 millimetres of freeboard in all other cases.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Freeboard requirements for slurry storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Freeboard requirements for slurry storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, channels, pipes, or reception pit may be situated within 10 metres of any inland or coastal waters which slurry could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum 10-metre separation distance for slurry infrastructure from waters
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum 10-metre separation distance for slurry infrastructure from waters

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry storage tanks, effluent tanks, channels, pipes and reception pits must be designed and constructed so that with proper maintenance they are likely to satisfy structural and impermeability requirements for at least 20 years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Design life requirement for slurry and effluent storage infrastructure
legislation_propositions.label: Design life requirement for slurry and effluent storage infrastructure

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank must extend beyond its walls.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Base extension requirement for non-impermeable slurry tank walls
legislation_propositions.label: Base extension requirement for non-impermeable slurry tank walls

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base must be provided with channels designed and constructed to collect any slurry which may escape from the tank.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Collection channel requirement for non-impermeable slurry tank base
legislation_propositions.label: Collection channel requirement for non-impermeable slurry tank base

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Adequate provision must be made for the drainage of slurry from the collection channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Drainage provision requirement from collection channels to effluent tank
legislation_propositions.label: Drainage provision requirement from collection channels to effluent tank

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where a slurry storage tank, effluent tank or reception pit is fitted with a drainage pipe, there must be two valves in series on the pipe, each capable of stopping the flow of slurry, and each valve must be kept shut and locked when not in use.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Two-valve requirement for drainage pipes on slurry/effluent tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Two-valve requirement for drainage pipes on slurry/effluent tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The two-valve requirement does not apply to a slurry storage tank which drains through the pipe into another slurry storage tank of equal or greater capacity or where the tops of the tanks are at the same level.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Exception to two-valve requirement for inter-tank drainage
legislation_propositions.label: Exception to two-valve requirement for inter-tank drainage

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage tank with walls made of earth must not be filled to a level that allows less than 750 millimetres of freeboard.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Freeboard requirement for earth-walled slurry storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Freeboard requirement for earth-walled slurry storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A slurry storage tank that does not have walls made of earth must not be filled to a level that allows less than 300 millimetres of freeboard.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Freeboard requirement for non-earth-walled slurry storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Freeboard requirement for non-earth-walled slurry storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A fuel oil storage area must be surrounded by a bund capable of retaining at least 110% of the capacity of the largest tank (where one tank exists) or the greater of 110% of the largest tank or 25% of total storage volume (where multiple tanks exist).
legislation_propositions.short_name: Bund retention capacity for fuel oil storage areas
legislation_propositions.label: Bund retention capacity for fuel oil storage areas

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The bund and base of a fuel oil storage area must be impermeable and designed to remain so for at least 20 years with proper maintenance.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability and durability requirements for fuel oil bunds
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability and durability requirements for fuel oil bunds

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel storage tank through which fuel oil can be discharged must be within the bund, discharge vertically downwards, and be shut and locked when not in use.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Requirements for taps and valves on fuel storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Requirements for taps and valves on fuel storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of a fuel oil storage area or its bund may be situated within 10 metres of any inland or coastal waters which fuel oil could enter if it escaped.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum separation distance from waters for fuel oil storage
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum separation distance from waters for fuel oil storage

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Requirements must be satisfied in relation to a fuel oil storage area.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fuel oil storage area requirements
legislation_propositions.label: Fuel oil storage area requirements

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A fuel oil storage area containing all fuel oil in one fuel storage tank shall be surrounded by a bund capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than 110 per cent of the capacity of the tank.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Bund capacity requirement for single fuel storage tank
legislation_propositions.label: Bund capacity requirement for single fuel storage tank

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A fuel oil storage area containing all fuel oil in more than one fuel storage tank shall be surrounded by a bund capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than the greater of: (i) 110 per cent of the capacity of the largest tank within the storage area; or (ii) 25 per cent of the total volume of such oil which could be stored in tanks within the area.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Bund capacity requirement for multiple fuel storage tanks
legislation_propositions.label: Bund capacity requirement for multiple fuel storage tanks

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: A fuel oil storage area in any other case shall be surrounded by a bund capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than the greater of: (i) 110 per cent of the capacity of the largest container within the storage area; or (ii) 25 per cent of the total volume of such oil at any time stored within the area.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Bund capacity requirement for fuel oil storage (other cases)
legislation_propositions.label: Bund capacity requirement for fuel oil storage (other cases)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The bund and the base of the storage area for slurry, manure or agricultural effluent shall be impermeable.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Impermeability requirement for bund and base
legislation_propositions.label: Impermeability requirement for bund and base

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: The bund and the base of the storage area for slurry, manure or agricultural effluent shall be designed and constructed so that with proper maintenance they are likely to remain impermeable for a period of at least 20 years.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Design and construction durability requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Design and construction durability requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Every part of any fuel storage tank shall be within the bund.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Fuel storage tank containment requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Fuel storage tank containment requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel oil tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be located within the bund.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Tap/valve location requirement (within bund)
legislation_propositions.label: Tap/valve location requirement (within bund)

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel oil tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be arranged to discharge vertically downwards.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Tap/valve discharge direction requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Tap/valve discharge direction requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel oil tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be shut and locked when not in use.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Tap/valve shut and locked requirement
legislation_propositions.label: Tap/valve shut and locked requirement

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: Where fuel from a tank is discharged through a permanently attached flexible pipe, the pipe shall be fitted with a tap or valve at its end which closes automatically when not in use.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Automatic closure tap/valve required on permanently attached flexible fuel discharge pipe
legislation_propositions.label: Automatic closure tap/valve required on permanently attached flexible fuel discharge pipe

legislation_propositions.proposition_text: No part of a fuel oil storage area or its enclosing bund may be situated within 10 metres of any inland or coastal waters which fuel oil could enter if it were to escape.
legislation_propositions.short_name: Minimum separation distance for fuel oil storage from waters
legislation_propositions.label: Minimum separation distance for fuel oil storage from waters

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: The Environment Agency has published its strategy EA2030, outlining clear goals to support healthy air, land, and water, while promoting nature's recovery, sustainable growth, and climate resilience.
The Water (Special Measures) Act 2025 introduces a statutory requirement for water companies to produce and publish annual Pollution Incident Reduction Plans (PIRPs).
Pollution Incident Reduction Plans (PIRPs) set out short-term, tactical actions to reduce the frequency and severity of pollution incidents.
Drainage and Wastewater Management Plans (DWMPs) are statutory plans that outline long-term strategies to improve and maintain a resilient drainage and wastewater system.
In 2024, over 800,000 tonnes of biosolids were produced by water companies in England, with 93% reused to support soil and agriculture.
All storm overflows in England now have Event Duration Monitors installed, with spill performance reports published annually.
The Water (Special Measures) Act 2025 requires water companies to install Event Duration Monitors on all emergency overflows at pumping stations: 50% by 2030 and full coverage by 2035.
The Water (Special Measures) Act 2025 will speed up the Environment Agency's enforcement response by imposing faster and more predictable civil penalties for less serious levels of offending.
The Water (Special Measures) Act 2025 provides the Environment Agency with the power to recover enforcement costs from water companies.
In 2024, serious pollution incidents from the water and sewerage sector increased by 60%, from 47 in 2023 to 75 in 2024.

In 2024, 1 of the 9 water and sewerage companies was rated as poor performing, 7 were rated as requiring improvement, and 1 was rated as industry leading under the Environmental Performance Assessment.
In 2024, farming activities caused 74 serious pollution incidents, increasing from 53 in 2023, representing 12% of all serious pollution incidents in 2024.
Dairy farming caused 48 serious pollution incidents in 2024, with 92% of dairy incidents involving silage or slurry.
In 2024, 51% of non-permitted farm inspections found non-compliance with environmental regulations, with insufficient slurry storage capacity identified at 33% of inspected farms.
The Slurry Infrastructure Grant aims to provide storage capacity of at least 6 months for beef and dairy cattle and 8 months for pigs.
The Slurry Infrastructure Grant provides partial funding to improve slurry storage, covering 50% of the costs of replacing, expanding, covering or building additional stores.

A farming business in Lancashire was prosecuted for two counts of illegal discharge and one count of failing to comply with slurry storage requirements, following investigation of two separate slurry incidents that polluted a local watercourse.
In 2024, the waste sector had the highest number of serious pollution incidents compared to other sectors regulated by the Environment Agency, accounting for 23% of all serious incidents.
In 2024, 146 serious pollution incidents were recorded from permitted and exempt waste management activities at 50 sites, a 57% increase compared with 93 incidents in 2023.
In 2024, 150 (91%) of persistent poor performer permits were in the waste sector; persistent poor performers are those with permits in bands D, E or F for 2 or more consecutive years.

In 2024, the waste sector demonstrated compliance with 91% of its permits (performance bands A and B), compared to 95% compliance for other industrial sectors regulated through the Environmental Permitting Regulations.
In 2024, prosecution cases against the waste sector led to total fines of around £320,000 and 37 custodial sentences.

The Environment Agency decided on 6 March 2025 to exercise its statutory powers under Regulation 57 of the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 to arrange steps to remove risks of serious pollution from Walleys Quarry Landfill Site.
Phase 1 rollout of digital waste tracking will become mandatory for all waste receiving sites from October 2026.
Waste crime is estimated to cost the country £1 billion per annum.
In 2024 to 2025, the Environment Agency stopped 743 illegal waste sites, of which 143 were high risk.
In 2024, the Environment Agency prevented the illegal export of 79,713 tonnes of waste.
In 2024, the UK Emissions Trading Scheme for installations and for aviation achieved compliance rates of 98%.

The Energy Savings Opportunities Scheme (ESOS) requires large companies and company groups to undertake an accredited energy assessment to identify opportunities to reduce energy usage and greenhouse gas emissions.

Under the Clean Heat Market Mechanism, manufacturers supplying gas and oil boilers in the UK market must meet targets for the installation of heat pumps in existing properties, set in proportion to their sales of fossil fuel boilers.

Operators using AI methods, including machine learning and large language models, must meet environmental compliance standards and provide clear documentation, validation, and auditable systems suited to the regulatory context.

During 2024, operators and permit holders in scope of climate change adaptation requirements were required to produce an initial risk assessment to understand the specific risks of climate change to and from their business.
In 2024, the Environment Agency brought 168 prosecution cases, 98 of which resulted in fines totalling £3.8 million.
In 2024, the Environment Agency issued 295 enforcement notices, almost double that in 2023.
In 2024, the Environment Agency accepted 52 enforcement undertakings totalling £4 million in donations to environmental projects or improvements.
In 2024, the Environment Agency imposed 1 civil sanction (variable monetary penalty) under the Water Resources Act for £19,778.
In 2024, 97% of permits regulated under the Environmental Permitting Regulations remained in the top three compliance bands (A to C), consistent with levels since 2013.
In 2024, there were 622 serious pollution incidents, 38% of which involved permitted activities.

The Environment Agency has begun publishing Compliance Assessment Reports (CARs) online for sectors regulated under the Environmental Permitting Regulations, replacing the previous request-based system.
Storm overflows account for 7% of waterbodies failing to reach Good Ecological Status.
Industrial sectors regulated under the Environmental Permitting Regulations were responsible for 15 serious pollution incidents in 2024, down from 33 in 2020, representing 2% of the national total.
In 2024, 25% of wastewater treatment works inspected had breaches of permit conditions.
The Environment Agency's water transformation programme has created over 500 roles focused on water industry regulation since it was set up in 2023.
The Environment Agency more than tripled the number of wastewater treatment works inspections to over 4,650 in 2024 to 2025.
In 2024 to 2025, the Environment Agency carried out 4,767 targeted farm inspections at 4,348 non-permitted farms.
In 2024, there were 978 inspections of farms permitted under the Environmental Permitting Regulations, of which 98% of permits were in the highest compliance bands (A and B).
Between 2022 and 2024 there were over 1,300 enforcement actions against farming businesses, with 15 being prosecutions.

An offender convicted of waste crime offences in 2021 was ordered in February 2025 to pay an additional £278,493 under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 after previously undeclared assets were discovered.
In 2024, the Environment Agency's water transformation work was funded through changes to charges applied to water quality discharge permits, increasing income by £51 million per year.
Industrial decarbonisation schemes administered by the Environment Agency cover over 40% of the UK's carbon emissions and have achieved high compliance rates.
In 2024, the UK ETS for installations operators delivered an 11.1 million tonne reduction of carbon dioxide compared to 2023.

The Environment Agency's Definition of Waste Service has provided 10 formal opinions this year, enabling 362,700 tonnes of material to be placed back on the market as non-waste, delivering annual savings to industry of over £19 million.
In 2024, 92% of water abstraction data returns were submitted digitally via the Manage your Water Abstraction Service.
The Environment Agency has established standard rules permits for low-risk research and development activities at permitted industrial installations, published in March 2025.
Each Mid Tier multi-year option and capital item has an associated code, name, and payment rate.

To receive support and approval from a Catchment Sensitive Farming Officer (CSFO), the options and capital items applied for must address the water or air pollutants identified as affecting that catchment or area.
An applicant must clearly show how water pollutants are currently reaching a watercourse or underground aquifer in order to receive CSFO support and approval.
An applicant must identify where ammonia emissions are coming from in order to receive CSFO support and approval for air quality options.
An applicant must show how the proposed work will prevent losses of water pollutants or ammonia in order to receive CSFO support and approval.
CSFO support will be targeted at farms where the largest improvements in water and air quality are likely to be achieved.
The impact of a water pollutant or ammonia on a sensitive protected site will be considered as part of CSFO support targeting.
An applicant must show that they have included a suitable range of options and capital items to prevent the pollutant reaching a watercourse or the atmosphere.
An applicant must agree with their CSFO how work is phased where it needs to be carried out over a number of years.
An applicant must contact their local CSFO at least 6 weeks before intending to submit an application, otherwise there is no guarantee the request will be considered.
An application receives a higher score if it meets local water and air quality objectives set out in the local Statement of Priorities.
Certain options and capital items require approval from a local CSFO before an applicant may apply for them.
If an applicant applies for CSFO-approval-required options or capital items without having that approval, those items will be removed from the application.
Land must be in a Countryside Stewardship High Priority Area for Water or Air Quality in order to be eligible for options and capital items requiring CSFO approval.
An applicant whose land is in a Countryside Stewardship High Priority Area for Water or Air and who wants CSFO support or approval must contact their local CSFO as early as possible.
An applicant must contact their local CSFO at least 6 weeks before intending to submit their application to request help or a visit.
When contacting a CSFO, an applicant must provide their name, address and postcode.
When contacting a CSFO, an applicant must provide their County Parish Holding (CPH) and Single Business Identifier (SBI) numbers.
When contacting a CSFO, an applicant must provide details of the capital items or options they are considering which will benefit water or air quality.
When contacting a CSFO, an applicant must provide information on water or air quality priorities on their farm.
When contacting a CSFO, an applicant must provide basic farm details such as size and enterprise type (for example, dairy, arable, poultry).

When contacting a CSFO, an applicant must provide information on how the pollutant is currently reaching a watercourse, or in the case of air where ammonia emissions are coming from, and how they intend to prevent this.
Any waste sent for biological treatment must be capable of being treated by the process.
Dilution is not considered a suitable waste treatment for biological treatment processes.
Biological processes can degrade complex synthetic organic substances.
The products resulting from biological degradation processes may pose a significant threat to human health and the environment.
Operators must fully characterise and assess all bespoke wastes before introducing them into a biological treatment process.
If an operator accepts a bespoke waste type, the site permit must include the relevant List of Waste (LoW) code and description as set out in technical guidance WM3.
Where an operator accepts similar bespoke waste from a different producer, that waste requires its own pre-acceptance assessment.
An operator may need to apply for a permit variation when accepting similar bespoke waste from a different producer, to ensure pre-acceptance processes are part of their operational techniques.
Operators may need to test the resulting outputs from biological treatment to ensure the material has been fully treated.
Biological treatment facilities may need to comply with The Animal By-Products (Enforcement) (England) Regulations 2013 to accept and treat animal by-products.
Animal by-products compliance for biological treatment facilities is regulated by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA).
Biological organic treatment facilities can be authorised to accept category 3 animal by-products.
AD plants where the only feedstock is grown energy crops or by-products from food waste production do not currently need an environmental permit or exemption for the digestion process.
Operators of AD plants using only energy crops or food waste by-products will need a permit for any combustion unit (engine, boiler or generator).
AD plants taking mixed feedstocks (energy crops, slurry, manure and waste) require an environmental permit for the digestion process.
AD plants taking mixed feedstocks (energy crops, slurry, manure and waste) require an environmental permit for any associated combustion unit or specified generator.
Materials produced incidentally to a process, such as clean-down or wash waters, leachates and liquors from feedstock storage, are waste.
Transfer and disposal of waste must comply with the duty of care code of practice under section 34(7) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990.
Measures with an equivalent annual net direct cost to business of below (plus or minus) £5 million are certified as being below de minimis under the Business Impact Target.
The Environment Agency created new Regulatory Position Statement RPS 233: Treating microbiological laboratory waste on the site where it is produced.
The Environment Agency created new Regulatory Position Statement RPS 234: Accepting, classifying and disposing of household packaging waste.
The Environment Agency created new Regulatory Position Statement RPS 235: Treating and using water that contains concrete and silt at construction sites.
The Environment Agency created new Regulatory Position Statement RPS 239: Temporary storage of recyclable waste at collection points for charities.
The Environment Agency revised Regulatory Position Statement RPS 55: Dewatering and depositing silts from sustainable drainage systems on land.
The Environment Agency withdrew Regulatory Position Statement RPS 56: Treatment by laboratory autoclave of containment level 1 to 3 microbiological waste on the premises it is produced.
The Environment Agency extended Regulatory Position Statement RPS 211: Excavated waste from utilities installation and repair.
The Environment Agency extended Regulatory Position Statement RPS 207: Classifying waste wood from mixed waste wood sources.
The Environment Agency created new Low Risk Waste Position LWRP 74: Burning dunnage packing material.
The Environment Agency created new Low Risk Waste Position LWRP 76: Recycling waste spectacles.
The Environment Agency published new standard rules SR2020 No 1 covering storage of Publicly Available Specification (PAS 107) certified clean cut tyre shred and chip at a port.
The Environment Agency published new guidance on healthcare waste: appropriate measures for permitted facilities.

The Environment Agency created a new regulatory position statement on slurry stores on permitted pig and poultry farms with less than 1% dry matter to ensure compliance with Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions.

The spreading of manure provides a route by which bacteria can pass from livestock to the natural environment, food crops, other animals and people.
Bacteria can develop resistance to antibiotics, leading to decreased treatment options for the infections they cause.
Attempts should be made to reduce the spread of antibiotic-resistant bacteria wherever possible.
The Animal by-products Regulation (EC1069/2009) defines manure as 'any excrement and/or urine of farmed animals other than farmed fish, with or without litter'.
Article 9 of the Animal by-products Regulation (EC1069/2009) classifies manure as a category 2 Animal by-product (ABP).
The Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) is responsible for enforcing the Animal by-products (ABP) regulation.
Where APHA identifies a risk to human or animal health associated with manure or slurry, specific control measures may be put in place, usually in relation to notifiable disease.
If APHA does not consider there to be a risk of spreading any serious, transmissible disease, manure can be applied to land without processing under Authorisation B1.
It is recommended that manure is stacked for a period of 8 weeks to reduce the number of bacteria that could present a danger to public or animal health.
Once a manure stack is formed, no further manure should be added to the stack for the entire 8-week period.
The manure stack should be sited so as to prevent livestock gaining access.
If possible, the manure stack should be sited on hard standing and covered once formed, to prevent access by wildlife (including birds).
Following the 8-week stacking period, manure can be spread on land.
Manure can be sent for composting at a designated facility.
There is no requirement to use an ABP-approved composting plant for the disposal of manure (unlike other materials such as food waste).
If the farm has adequate storage capacity, it is recommended that slurry is held for a period of 3 months prior to spreading on land.
During the 3-month slurry holding period, no further slurry is to be added.
Both slurry and manure can be sent to an anaerobic digestion plant.
There is no requirement to use an ABP-approved anaerobic digestion site for the disposal of manure (unlike other materials such as food waste).
It is best practice to spread slurry or manure on arable land rather than pasture which will be grazed or cropped for animal feed, in order to reduce transmission of bacteria to other animals.

If manure or slurry is applied to grazing land or land cropped for feed production, it is recommended that grazing or cropping does not take place for a period of at least 8 weeks, to reduce the risk of spreading antibiotic-resistant bacteria to livestock.
Injecting slurry rather than top spreading reduces the spread of resistance by reducing runoff and minimising wildlife exposure.

It is advisable to take appropriate hygiene and bio-security precautions when spreading or handling manure, for example wearing outer clothing and waterproof footwear which can be cleaned and disinfected, wearing gloves, and hand washing.
Manure must not be stored or treated anywhere near food crops which are eaten without cooking, such as salads.
Authorisation D10 allows the transport of manure between two points located on the same farm, or between farms and users of manure.
Manure being transported under Authorisation D10 should be transported in covered leak-proof containers in conditions which prevent unacceptable risks to animal and public health.
Additional requirements apply for farms or fields located in nitrogen vulnerable zones.
Stacked manure and slurry that has been batch-stored for a minimum period of 6 months prior to spreading may be applied to land used to grow ready to eat crops any time before drilling or planting.

Composted solid manure or lime-treated slurry that has been stored to allow maturation for at least 3 months prior to spreading may be applied to land used to grow ready to eat crops any time before drilling or planting.
Solid manure and slurry that is untreated or does not meet the specified treatment conditions should not be applied to land used to grow ready to eat crops within 12 months of harvest.

Manure or slurry applied to land used to grow ready to eat vegetables should be incorporated into the soil as soon as is practicable, to reduce the potential for direct crop contamination and to reduce odour and ammonia emissions.

Digestate from slurry or manure processed in an anaerobic digestion plant that complies with BSI PAS 110 requirements may be applied to land used to grow ready to eat crops any time before drilling and planting.
Natural England will continue to deliver the £30 million Nutrient Mitigation Scheme in line with the Environment Secretary's direction of 28 July 2022.
Nutrient mitigation credits for 4,200 new homes have already been provided by the Nutrient Mitigation Scheme in the Tees and Cleveland Coast catchment.
The Nutrient Mitigation Scheme will continue to operate on the principle of complementing locally and privately led mitigation schemes, rather than crowding out these schemes.
Natural England will continue to provide advice and guidance to other scheme operators, helping to secure and grow the potential pipeline of credits.

The £110 million Local Nutrient Mitigation Fund will enable local authorities to boost the supply of mitigation by investing in innovative mitigation schemes and enabling additional mitigation credits.

Funding from the Local Nutrient Mitigation Fund will be recycled locally until nutrient mitigation is no longer needed, at which point it will be invested in measures to help restore the relevant Habitats Sites.
DLUHC has confirmed the first tranche of capital funding with up to £57 million of funding to the 8 successful bids under the Local Nutrient Mitigation Fund.
DLUHC has confirmed a second round of Nutrient Support Funding with another £100,000 to a lead authority for substantive catchments (those over 10,000 hectares in size).
Round 2 of the Local Nutrient Mitigation Fund is open to Expressions of Interest until 26 April 2024.

The Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023 created a new duty for water companies in designated catchments to ensure wastewater treatment works serving a population equivalent over 2,000 meet specified nutrient removal standards.

Competent authorities (including local planning authorities) considering planning proposals for development draining via a sewer to a wastewater treatment works subject to the upgrade duty are required to consider that the nutrient pollution standard will be met by the upgrade date for the purposes of Habitats Regulations Assessments.

On 25 January 2024, the Secretary of State for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs designated 16 catchments in which water companies are required to upgrade wastewater treatment works before 1 April 2030.
A limited exemption process for wastewater treatment works exemptions will be completed by 1 April 2024.

Wastewater treatment works exemptions confirmed by 1 April 2024 may affect the levels of nutrient mitigation that development must secure when connecting to specific wastewater treatment works in some catchments.
Planning decisions must continue to be taken based on material planning considerations.
The government will invest £200 million in grants for improved slurry storage infrastructure and equipment over the agricultural transition period.
The government will commit £25 million to a new nutrient management theme within the Farming Innovation Programme to help farmers manage plant and soil nutrients.
The government will introduce payment premiums into environmental land management schemes in 2024, including for options that provide benefits for water quality.

The government will continue to conduct at least 4,000 risk-based inspections on farms each year to ensure slurry and other pollutants are handled in a way that minimises pollution of the water environment.
The government will consult on mandating Sustainable Drainage Solutions for relevant new developments, subject to a threshold, to reduce urban run-off and pressure on storm overflows and flood risk.

Defra launched an additional round of the Natural Environment Investment Readiness Fund, which opened for applications on 11 December, to help farmers address barriers to accessing private investment for nature's recovery including through nutrient mitigation projects.
A river basin is the area of land from which all surface water run-off flows through a sequence of streams, rivers and possibly lakes into the sea at a single river mouth or estuary.

A river basin district includes the area of land and sea made up of one or more neighbouring river basins together with their associated groundwaters and coastal waters, covering one nautical mile from the coast.
The Water Environment (Water Framework Directive) (England and Wales) Regulations 2017 require the preparation and publication of river basin management plans.

The Water Environment (Water Framework Directive) (England and Wales) Regulations 2017 require the setting of environmental objectives for groundwater and surface waters, including estuaries and coastal waters.
The Water Environment (Water Framework Directive) (England and Wales) Regulations 2017 require the devising and implementing of programmes of measures to meet environmental objectives.
Under the WFD Regulations, a river basin management plan must be developed for each river basin district.
Under the WFD Regulations, a river basin management plan must be reviewed and updated every 6 years.
River basin management plans were first published in December 2009, updated in February 2016, and updated again in December 2022.
The river basin management plans will be reviewed and updated again by December 2027.
All public bodies are under a duty to 'have regard to' the river basin management plans.
The Environment Agency and Natural England produce diffuse water pollution plans for some habitats sites.
'Habitats sites' refers to 'European sites' and 'European marine sites' as defined in regulation 8 of the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended).
New activities or developments must comply with constraints identified in river basin management plans.

The Marine Management Organisation issues marine licences for activities in and around the estuaries and sea of English waters, including construction, dredging, removal, and deposit of substances and objects at sea.
The Environment Act 2021 requires the government to always have an Environmental Improvement Plan in place.
The government must review its Environmental Improvement Plan every 5 years.
The WFD Regulations require river basin planning data to be presented at river basin district level.
The 25 Year Environment Plan was designated as the first statutory Environmental Improvement Plan under the Environment Act 2021.
